definition_zh: 使熟悉；使认识；介绍
definition_en: to make someone familiar with something or with another person
core_image: 有人牵着你的手，把一张张陌生的脸介绍给你
scene: 向导先把当地的规矩一条条讲给我们听。 The guide acquainted us with the local rules.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquaint 是「使熟悉」（第 1 个义项：让人了解某事）；句意是向导让我们熟悉了当地规矩。

collocations.phrase: acquaint a friend with the facts

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「熟人；了解」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「熟悉的」
由名词再加抽象名词后缀构成，义为「相识关系」

senses.title: To make familiar with something
senses.definition: to give someone knowledge of a subject, place or rule
senses.definitionCN: 让某人了解某个主题、地方或规矩
senses.example: The manual acquaints new staff with safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 手册让新员工熟悉安全规则。
senses.why: The Latin base cognoscere means to know, so the verb is literally to bring someone into knowledge of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 cognoscere 意为「知道」，所以这个动词字面上就是把某人带进对某事的了解里。

senses.title: To introduce people to each other
senses.definition: to bring two people together so that they come to know one another
senses.definitionCN: 把两个人带到一起，使他们彼此认识
senses.example: Their host acquainted the two guests before dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 主人在饭前介绍两位客人相识。
senses.why: Knowing a fact and knowing a person use the same verb because both begin with a first meeting and a name.
senses.whyCN: 认识一件事与认识一个人用同一个动词，因为两者都始于一次初见和一个名字。

intro.en: The word came through Old French from a Latin verb of knowing.
intro.cn: 这个词经由古法语，来自一个表示「知道」的拉丁动词。

items.en: cognoscere meant to get to know or to learn.
items.cn: cognoscere 意为逐渐知道、了解到。

items.en: accognitare added a prefix of direction to the same root.
items.cn: accognitare 在同一个词根前加了表示方向的前缀。

items.en: acointier meant to make someone known to another.
items.cn: acointier 意为使某人被另一人认识。

items.en: acquaint entered English as a verb of familiarizing.
items.cn: acquaint 在十三世纪进入英语，是表示「使熟悉」的动词。

items.en: be acquainted with is now far commoner than the active form.
items.cn: 如今 be acquainted with 这一说法远比其他主动形式常见。

note.en: The first group is the acquaint family; the second is other verbs of familiarizing.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquaint 词族；第二组是别的表示使熟悉的动词。

examples.en: She soon became acquainted with the neighbours.
examples.cn: 她很快就和邻居们熟悉了。

branches.cn: 一个动词兼管对事与对人的认识

intro.en: A Latin prefix and a knowing root form the verb, which reached English through French.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁前缀和一个「知道」词根构成这个动词，再经法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: cognoscere, to know, also gives recognize, cognition and notice.
latinIntro.cn: cognoscere（知道）也给出 recognize、cognition 与 notice。

definition_zh: 隐藏；隐瞒；掩盖
definition_en: to hide something or keep it secret
core_image: 一只手把一枚硬币悄悄塞到桌布下面
scene: 她把礼物藏在衣柜最上层，等生日那天再拿出来。 He tried to conceal the gift behind the coats.
sceneCN: 这里 conceal 指「藏起」（第 1 个义项：放到看不见的地方）；句意是他想把礼物藏在大衣后面。

senses.title: Hide from sight
senses.definition: to put something where it cannot be seen
senses.definitionCN: 把某物放到看不见的地方
senses.example: The camera was concealed in a clock.
senses.exampleCN: 摄像头被藏在一只钟里。
senses.why: The word begins with physical hiding, a thing placed out of view.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指物理上的隐藏，把东西放到视线之外。

senses.title: Keep a fact secret
senses.definition: to keep information from other people
senses.definitionCN: 不让他人知道某些信息
senses.example: She concealed her disappointment.
senses.exampleCN: 她隐瞒了自己的失望。
senses.why: A feeling or fact can be hidden just as a box can be hidden.
senses.whyCN: 情绪或事实能像盒子一样被藏起来。

intro.en: Conceal comes from Latin concelare, to hide completely, built from com-, fully, and celare, to hide.
intro.cn: conceal 来自拉丁语 concelare（完全藏起），由 com-（完全）与 celare（隐藏）构成。

items.en: Celare meant to hide or to keep secret.
items.cn: celare 意为隐藏或保守秘密。

items.en: Concelare strengthened the verb into hiding completely.
items.cn: concelare 把动词强化为完全藏起来。

items.en: Old French concealer carried the strong sense of covering up.
items.cn: 古法语 concealer 保留了严密遮掩的强烈意味。

items.en: English conceal first meant to cover or to keep from sight.
items.cn: 英语 conceal 最初指遮盖或不让看见。

items.en: It now covers hiding facts, feelings and objects alike.
items.cn: 如今它同样覆盖隐藏事实、情绪与物件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to conceal, and the meaning group names other words for keeping something out of view.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 conceal 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他把东西藏起来的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a coin slipping under a tablecloth, then move to secrets and to hidden feelings.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一枚硬币滑到桌布下开始，再走到秘密与被藏起的情绪。

normal.en: Con- makes the hiding complete, and celare is to hide, so conceal is to hide fully.
normal.cn: con- 让隐藏变得彻底，celare 是隐藏，所以 conceal 就是完全藏起来。

normal.en: A concealed camera is there but not seen.
normal.cn: 隐藏的摄像头在那里，却看不见。

normal.en: You can conceal a fact with silence as easily as with a lie.
normal.cn: 用沉默隐瞒事实，和用谎话一样容易。

normal.en: Conceal is more formal than hide, and often suggests intent.
normal.cn: conceal 比 hide 更正式，常暗示有意为之。

normal.en: The noun is concealment, the state of being kept from view.
normal.cn: 名词是 concealment，即被藏在视线之外的状态。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pushing a coin under a cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把硬币推到布下面。

abstract.en: Picture a smile that covers a whole bad day.
abstract.cn: 想象一个笑容盖住了整个糟糕的日子。

abstract.en: Picture a door painted the same colour as the wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门刷成和墙一样的颜色。

examples.en: He concealed the key under a loose stone.
examples.cn: 他把钥匙藏在一块松动的石头下。

examples.en: She could not conceal her surprise.
examples.cn: 她掩饰不住惊讶。

examples.en: The report concealed several important facts.
examples.cn: 这份报告隐瞒了几个重要事实。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conceal 记成 con（完全）加 ceal（藏）：把东西完全藏起来，就是隐藏、隐瞒。

root: 源自拉丁语 concelare（com 完全 + celare 隐藏），本义是完全藏起，后指隐藏物件与隐瞒事实、情绪。

sensesIntro.en: From an object put out of sight, to a fact kept from other people.
sensesIntro.cn: 从被放到看不见处的物件，到不让他人知道的事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand sliding a coin under the tablecloth.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把硬币悄悄推到桌布下面。

branches.en: Physical hiding is the first and most literal sense.
branches.cn: 物理隐藏是第一个也最字面的义项。

branches.en: Information can be treated as an object placed out of view.
branches.cn: 信息可以被当作放到视线之外的物件。

branches.en: A concealed weapon is a legal and physical matter.
branches.cn: 隐藏的武器既涉及法律也涉及物理。

branches.en: A concealed feeling stays inside the person.
branches.cn: 被隐瞒的情绪留在人心里。

branches.en: Both senses depend on someone not seeing or not knowing.
branches.cn: 两个义项都依赖别人看不到或不知道。

intro.en: Conceal is built on Latin com-, fully, plus celare, to hide, through the French form concealer.
intro.cn: conceal 由拉丁语 com-（完全）与 celare（隐藏）构成，经法语 concealer 进入英语。

latinIntro.en: The Latin hide base cel- also survives in clandestine and cellar.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的隐藏词基 cel- 还留在 clandestine 与 cellar 中。

definition_zh: 顺利地；平稳地；流畅地
definition_en: without problems, in a steady way, or in a flowing way
core_image: 列车沿着轨道平稳地驶过
scene: 会议进行得很顺利。 The meeting went smoothly.
sceneCN: 这里 smoothly 是「顺利地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：会议进行得很顺利。

senses.title: Without problems
senses.definition: without difficulties or delays
senses.definitionCN: 没有困难或延误
senses.example: The meeting went smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 会议进行得很顺利。
senses.why: This is the main event sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要的事件义项。

senses.title: In a steady way
senses.definition: moving in a steady way without shaking
senses.definitionCN: 以稳定、无晃动的方式移动
senses.example: The train ran smoothly along the track.
senses.exampleCN: 列车沿着轨道平稳行驶。
senses.why: An even surface gives an even motion.
senses.whyCN: 平整的表面带来平稳的运动。

senses.title: In a flowing way
senses.definition: in a way that flows easily, used of speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 以顺畅流动的方式，指说话或写作
senses.example: She speaks English smoothly.
senses.exampleCN: 她英语说得很流畅。
senses.why: Language can be smooth like a surface.
senses.whyCN: 语言可以像表面一样平滑。

intro.en: Smoothly was formed from smooth with the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: smoothly 由 smooth 加上副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Smoth meant free from roughness.
items.cn: smoth 意为不粗糙的。

items.en: The adverb form appeared later.
items.cn: 副词形式后来出现。

items.en: It described calm movement.
items.cn: 它形容平稳的运动。

items.en: It described trouble-free events.
items.cn: 它形容没有麻烦的事件。

items.en: It described flowing speech.
items.cn: 它形容流畅的言语。

note.en: Smoothly is compared with look-alike words and words for easy movement.
note.cn: 把 smoothly 与形近词以及表示顺畅移动的词作比较。

definition_zh: 责骂；训斥；唠叨地责备
definition_en: to speak angrily to someone because of a fault, or to criticize them repeatedly
core_image: 母亲叉着腰站在碎花瓶旁，指着低头认错的孩子训话
scene: 孩子打碎花瓶后，母亲责备了他。 The mother scolded the boy for breaking the vase.
sceneCN: 这里 scold 是「责骂；训斥」（第 1 个义项）；句意：孩子打碎花瓶后，母亲责备了他。

senses.title: To reprove angrily
senses.definition: to speak angrily to someone because they have done wrong
senses.definitionCN: 因某人做错事而生气地对其说话
senses.example: She scolded him for being late.
senses.exampleCN: 她因他迟到而责备他。
senses.why: The core sense is a sharp spoken reproof.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是严厉的口头责备。

senses.title: To criticize repeatedly
senses.definition: to keep finding fault with someone in a nagging way
senses.definitionCN: 以唠叨的方式不断挑某人的错
senses.example: Stop scolding me about the dishes.
senses.exampleCN: 别老为洗碗的事责备我。
senses.why: The sense extends from one reproof to constant fault-finding.
senses.whyCN: 词义从一次责备延伸到不断挑错。

intro.en: Scold may come from Old Norse skald, a poet or satirist, and first named a quarrelsome person.
intro.cn: scold 可能与古诺尔斯语 skald（诗人、讽刺者）有关，最初指爱争吵责骂的人。

items.en: Skald meant a poet, often one who mocked others.
items.cn: skald 指诗人，常是讽刺他人者。

items.en: Scold named a person who quarrelled noisily.
items.cn: scold 指大声争吵的人。

items.en: The noun became a verb meaning to use harsh words.
items.cn: 名词转为动词，意为使用严厉言语。

items.en: The verb narrowed to reproving someone for a fault.

items.en: Scold now means to criticize someone angrily.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scold 意为生气地批评某人。

note.en: Scold is compared with similar-looking words and with verbs for criticism.
note.cn: 把 scold 与形近词以及表示批评的动词作比较。

branches.en: One sharp reproof for a mistake.

branches.en: Constant fault-finding that wears people down.

branches.en: Both senses use words as correction.
branches.cn: 两个义项都用言语进行纠正。

branches.en: The difference is frequency and tone.
branches.cn: 区别在于频率与语气。

branches.en: A reproof can become a habit.
branches.cn: 责备可能变成习惯。

intro.en: Scold forms nouns and adverbs for the act of reproof.
intro.cn: scold 构成表示责备行为的名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic in origin; it has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词源自日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.exampleCN: 那个爱骂人的人天天抱怨。

items.example: Scoldings did not change his habits.
items.exampleCN: 责骂没有改变他的习惯。

items.example: She spoke scoldingly to the child.

definition_zh: 蒸气；水汽；雾气；（物理上）气态物质；美式拼作 vapor
definition_en: a mass of tiny drops or gas, such as water in the air, that can be seen or felt
core_image: 一壶开水冒着白气，气一碰到窗玻璃就凝成水珠
scene: 清晨的湖面浮着一层薄薄的白气，太阳一照便慢慢散开。 Thick vapour rose from the hot spring and hid the rocks behind it.
sceneCN: 这里 vapour 是「蒸气、水汽」（第 1 个义项：水变成的气体或细小水滴）；句意为温泉升起浓重的水汽，把后面的岩石遮住了。水壶上升腾又凝成珠的白气，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 名词：蒸气、水汽；雾气；气态物质（英式拼写，美式为 vapor）

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「雾化器、蒸发器」
形容词，义为「雾状的、含汽的、缥缈的」
动词，义为「蒸发」，同源于拉丁语 vapor 与 ex-

senses.title: Water in the air
senses.titleCN: 水汽：从水面升起的白气
senses.definition: tiny drops or invisible gas from water, often visible as mist
senses.definitionCN: 水形成的细小水滴或气体，常以雾状可见
senses.example: Thick vapour rose from the hot spring and hid the rocks behind it.
senses.exampleCN: 温泉升起浓重的水汽，把后面的岩石遮住了。
senses.why: Latin vapor named steam or exhalation; the word has always pictured something rising off a wet surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vapor 指蒸汽或呼气；这个词一直带着从湿面上腾起的画面。

senses.title: A gas in science
senses.titleCN: 气态：物理上区别于液体固体的状态
senses.definition: the gaseous state of a substance that is liquid or solid at room temperature
senses.definitionCN: 常温下是液体或固体的物质的气态形式
senses.example: At this pressure the fuel turns into vapour before it burns.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个压力下，燃油在燃烧前就变成气态。
senses.why: Science sharpened the old picture into a term: vapour is a substance in its gas phase.
senses.whyCN: 科学把旧画面锐化成一个术语：vapour 是物质处在气态阶段。

senses.title: Mist on glass
senses.titleCN: 玻璃上的雾气：冷凝的一层水膜
senses.definition: condensed droplets that cloud a cold surface
senses.definitionCN: 凝在冷表面上形成一层模糊水膜的小水珠
senses.example: The bathroom mirror was covered in vapour after the hot shower.
senses.exampleCN: 热水澡后浴室的镜子上蒙了一层水汽。
senses.why: The same vapour that rises goes back to liquid on a cold surface; the word covers both the rising and the settling.
senses.whyCN: 升起的水汽在冷面上变回液体；这个词既指升腾也指凝结。

senses.title: Figurative haze
senses.titleCN: 缥缈：像雾一样抓不住的东西
senses.definition: something vague and fleeting, compared to mist
senses.definitionCN: 像雾一样模糊而短暂的东西
senses.example: His plans melted into vapour as the money ran out.
senses.exampleCN: 钱一花完，他的计划就化作一阵虚无。
senses.why: Mist can hide things without destroying them; the metaphor borrows this to describe hopes and promises.
senses.whyCN: 雾能遮住东西却不破坏它；比喻借这一点来形容希望与承诺。

intro.en: Vapour comes from the Latin noun vapor, steam or exhalation, and keeps its American and British spellings side by side.
intro.cn: vapour 来自拉丁语名词 vapor「蒸汽、呼气」，英式与美式两种拼写至今并存。

items.en: Latin vapor meant steam, exhalation or a light mist rising from something wet.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vapor 指蒸汽、呼出的气，或从湿物上腾起的薄雾。

items.en: Old French took the word as vapour, keeping the meaning of rising steam.
items.cn: 古法语借作 vapour，保留了升腾蒸汽之义。

items.en: English adopted the French form in the late Middle Ages for steam and cloudy air.
items.cn: 英语在中山后期借入法语形式，用于蒸汽与浑浊的空气。

items.en: American usage dropped the u under Noah Webster´s influence, giving vapor, while Britain kept vapour.
items.cn: 美式在韦伯斯特影响下删去 u，写成 vapor，英国则保留 vapour。

items.en: In physics the word settled down as the gas phase of a substance that is normally liquid or solid.
items.cn: 在物理学里，这个词定型为常温液或固体的气态阶段。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the vapor- family; the near-meaning group holds clouds of damp air.
note.cn: 形近组收 vapor- 词族；近义组收表示潮湿空气与云的词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蒸气」，同一名词的美式拼写。

entries.definition: The verb for turning into vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「汽化」，由本词加 -ize 构成。

entries.definition: Full of vapour or mist, or figuratively vague.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「雾状的、缥缈的」。

entries.definition: To pass off as vapour; uses the same Latin base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「蒸发」，用同一个拉丁词基。

entries.definition: Water vapour at high temperature, often visible as a white jet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蒸汽」，高温水蒸气，常呈白色喷射状。

entries.definition: Fine droplets hanging in the air, lighter than fog.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「薄雾」，比雾更轻。

entries.definition: Thick cloud near the ground that cuts visibility down.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「浓雾」，贴近地面、遮挡视线的云团。

entries.definition: Any substance in the air-like state, a wider scientific term.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「气体」，更宽泛的科学术语。

normalIntro.en: The hooks rely on the kettle picture and on real phrases such as water vapour.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子依靠水壶画面的意象以及 water vapour 这样的真实搭配。

normal.en: Vapour and vapor are the same word; only the u differs.
normal.cn: vapour 与 vapor 是同一个词，只差一个 u。

normal.en: Water vapour is invisible; what you see above a kettle is condensed droplets.
normal.cn: 水蒸气本身不可见，水壶上方看到的是凝结成的小水珠。

normal.en: A vapour trail is the white line a jet leaves across the sky.
normal.cn: vapour trail 是飞机在天空留下的白线。

normal.en: Add -ize and vapour becomes the verb vaporize, to turn into gas.
normal.cn: 加上 -ize，vapour 就变成动词 vaporize「汽化」。

normal.en: Mist on a cold mirror is vapour going back to liquid water.
normal.cn: 冷镜子上的水汽，就是汽又变回了液态水。

abstract.en: Vapour is matter in its most fugitive form: present, yet ready to be gone.
abstract.cn: 汽是物质最易逃逸的形态：明明在场，却随时准备消失。

abstract.en: The word moves easily from a physical cloud to a mental one, because mist already hides things.
abstract.cn: 这个词很自然地从物理的雾走到心里的雾，因为雾本来就会遮东西。

abstract.en: Water crosses three names in one day: ice, water, vapour; the last one is the one that travels.
abstract.cn: 水一天里走过三个名字：冰、水、汽；最后那个才是会旅行的。

examples.en: Water vapour rises from the sea and forms clouds.
examples.cn: 水汽从海面升起，聚成云。

examples.en: A cloud of vapour hung over the boiling pot.
examples.cn: 沸腾的锅上方悬着一团水汽。

examples.en: The cold window was soon covered with vapour.
examples.cn: 冰冷的窗户很快蒙上了一层水汽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「为泼」——水被熬得为泼（蒸发）出去，只剩气：蒸气

root: 源自拉丁语名词 vapor「蒸汽、呼气」，经古法语 vapour 进入英语；美式拼作 vapor；同族词有 vaporize、vaporous、evaporate。

sensesIntro.en: Vapour starts as visible steam, narrows into a scientific gas phase, and ends up as figurative mist.
sensesIntro.cn: vapour 从看得见的蒸汽出发，缩成一个科学上的气态术语，最后化作比喻的雾。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white air lifts off hot water and turns back into drops on cold glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：白气从热水上升起，又在冷玻璃上变回水珠。

branches.en: AIR LINE: visible vapour above hot water.
branches.cn: 空气线：热水上方可见的水汽。

branches.en: SCIENCE LINE: a substance in its gas state.
branches.cn: 科学线：物质的气态形式。

branches.en: GLASS LINE: drops settle on cold surfaces.
branches.cn: 玻璃线：水珠凝在冷表面上。

branches.en: METAPHOR LINE: plans that melt into haze.
branches.cn: 比喻线：计划化成一片迷雾。

branches.en: CONTRAST: vapour is invisible, mist is what you see.
branches.cn: 对照线：水汽本身不可见，雾是你看见的东西。

intro.en: Vapour is a whole Latin noun; its English relatives come from adding standard endings.
intro.cn: vapour 是一个完整的拉丁名词，英语亲属词都由标准词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is vapor, with the verb evaporare formed from ex- plus vapor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语基础是 vapor，动词 evaporare 由前缀 ex- 加 vapor 构成。

items.example: It is the whole base of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词的完整词基。

items.example: It shows the word in use.
It is the most common pairing.

definition_zh: 滴下；滴水；水滴；滴水声；输液
definition_en: to fall in small drops, or a small drop of liquid
core_image: 水龙头下悬着一颗水珠，迟迟不肯落
scene: 夜里水管没拧紧，浴室里每隔一会儿就响一声。 The tap began to drip onto the tiles.
sceneCN: 这里 drip 是「滴下」（第 1 个义项）；句意是水龙头开始往瓷砖上滴水。

pos.zh: 名词：水滴；滴水声；滴注器

derivatives.zh: 由 drip 加 -ing 构成，义为「滴落的液体；滴下的油脂」
由 drip 加 -y 构成，义为「湿淋淋的」

senses.title: To fall in small drops
senses.definition: to fall slowly in small drops, or to let small drops fall
senses.definitionCN: 以小水滴的形式缓慢落下，或让水滴落下
senses.example: Water dripped from the leaking pipe all night.
senses.exampleCN: 水管漏了，整夜都在滴水。
senses.why: The word is imitative of the sound and motion of a drop, so the verb simply repeats what a dripping tap does.
senses.whyCN: 这个词模仿水滴落下的声音与动作，所以动词只是把「滴水的龙头」所做的事说出来。

senses.title: A single drop of liquid
senses.definition: a small drop of liquid that falls or hangs
senses.definitionCN: 落下或悬着的一小滴液体
senses.example: A drip hung under the tap for a long time.
senses.exampleCN: 一滴水在龙头下面挂了很久。
senses.why: The thing that falls takes the same name as the falling, so one hanging drop is a drip.
senses.whyCN: 落下的东西沿用了落下的动作之名，所以一颗悬着的水滴也叫 drip。

senses.title: A slow supply through a tube
senses.definition: a device or treatment that passes liquid into the body slowly, drop by drop
senses.definitionCN: 把液体一滴一滴缓慢送入体内的装置或疗法
senses.example: The nurse set up a drip for the patient.
senses.exampleCN: 护士给病人挂上了输液。
senses.why: Medical feeding copies the tap: liquid is delivered one drop at a time, so the equipment is also a drip.
senses.whyCN: 医疗输注照搬了水龙头的节奏：一滴一滴地送液，所以这套装置也叫 drip。

intro.en: Drip is an imitative English word, probably from a Scandinavian source, shaped by the sound of falling drops.
intro.cn: drip 是模仿性的英语词，可能来自斯堪的纳维亚语，形态受水滴落下的声音影响。

items.en: A Norse verb for dripping probably fed the English word; the link is likely but not certain.
items.cn: 一个表示「滴落」的诺斯语动词很可能滋养了这个英语词；联系合理但不完全确定。

items.en: An Old English word for a drop existed alongside, and the two forms influenced each other.
items.cn: 古英语里另有表示「一滴」的词，两种形式互相影响。

items.en: Drippen named the slow falling of liquid and echoed the sound of the event.
items.cn: drippen 指液体的缓慢下落，并在读音上模仿这个过程。

items.en: The noun appeared for a single hanging drop; early records are roughly dated.
items.cn: 名词出现，指一颗悬着的水滴；早期记录的年代只能大致推定。

items.en: The medical drip sense followed in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
items.cn: 医学上的输液义在十九至二十世纪出现。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the stem; the near-meaning group separates dropping from leaking.
note.cn: 形近组共享词干；近义组把「滴」与「漏」分开。

entries.definition: Liquid that falls in drops, or the fat from roasted meat.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「滴落的液体；烤肉滴下的油脂」，由 drip 加 -ing 构成。

entries.definition: Wet enough to drip.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「湿淋淋的」，由 drip 加 -y 构成。

entries.definition: A small round amount of liquid, or to let something fall.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「一滴；落下」，与 drip 同族近义。

entries.definition: To let liquid escape through a hole, often continuously.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「漏」，强调从孔洞持续渗出。

entries.definition: To flow slowly in a thin stream, not in separate drops.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「细流」，是细线状而非一滴一滴。

entries.definition: To flow slowly through a porous material.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「渗」，强调透过材料缓慢扩散。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the drop shape and the sound, then extend to medical feeding.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子守住水滴的形状与声音，再延伸到医疗输注。

normal.en: Say drip slowly and you hear the drop land.
normal.cn: 把 drip 慢慢读出来，就能听见水滴落地的声音。

normal.en: A drip is both the falling and the drop that falls.
normal.cn: drip 既是「落下」这个动作，也是落下的那滴水。

normal.en: A dripping tap repeats the same small sound all night.
normal.cn: 漏水的龙头整夜重复同一个细微的声响。

normal.en: A medical drip feeds you one drop at a time.
normal.cn: 输液的 drip 是一滴一滴地给你送液。

normal.en: Drip, drop and trickle form a family of water sounds.
normal.cn: drip、drop、trickle 组成一族「水声」词。

abstract.en: Picture a bead of water swelling under a tap.
abstract.cn: 想象水龙头下鼓起的一颗水珠。

abstract.en: Picture a dark stain spreading on a ceiling.
abstract.cn: 想象天花板上逐渐扩大的深色水渍。

abstract.en: Picture a clear tube hanging beside a hospital bed.
abstract.cn: 想象病床旁垂着的一根透明细管。

examples.en: Rain water dripped from the edge of the roof.
examples.cn: 雨水从屋檐边缘滴下来。

examples.en: He wiped a drip of paint from the floor.
examples.cn: 他擦掉了地板上的一滴油漆。

examples.en: The patient was on a drip for two days.
examples.cn: 病人挂了两天输液。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「滴扑」——水滴一下一下地扑向地面，这个声音就是 drip。

root: 模仿水滴声与滴落动作的英语词，可能受古诺斯语表示「滴落」的动词影响，并与古英语里表示「一滴」的词互相影响，具体来源不完全确定。由「滴落」转指「一滴水」，再延伸为医学上的「滴注、输液」。

sensesIntro.en: One falling drop supplies a verb, a countable drop, and the tube that feeds liquid by the drop.
sensesIntro.cn: 一颗落下的水珠，给出了动词、可数的一滴，以及按滴送液的管子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bead of water swelling under a tap.
core.cn: 核心意象：水龙头下正在鼓起的一颗水珠。

branches.en: ACTION: the verb is the physical falling of drops.
branches.cn: 动作线：动词就是水滴落下的物理过程，即第一个义项。

branches.en: OBJECT: a single bead takes the name of the falling.
branches.cn: 物体线：一颗水珠沿用了「落」的名称，即第二个义项。

branches.en: MEDICINE: the same drop-by-drop rhythm feeds a patient.
branches.cn: 医疗线：同样的「一滴一滴」节奏被用来给病人送液，即第三个义项。

branches.en: The falling and the drop are one event split into verb and noun.
branches.cn: 落下与水滴，是同一件事分成动词与名词。

branches.en: A leaking tap and a hospital drip share the same slow rhythm.
branches.cn: 漏水的龙头与医院输液，共享同一种缓慢节奏。

intro.en: Drip is a short imitative stem that takes -ing and -y and builds compounds.
intro.cn: drip 是短小的拟声词干，可接 -ing、-y 并参与复合。

latinIntro.en: No Latin element is involved; the word is English with a possible Norse nudge.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁成分；这个词属英语，可能受过诺斯语一点影响。

items.example: The Norse verb may have reinforced the English form.
items.exampleCN: 这个诺斯语动词可能强化了英语形式。

items.example: A tap can drip all night.
A pipe may drip at a joint.

derivatives.zh: 由 drip 加 -ing 构成，义为「滴落的液体」
由 drip 加 -y 构成，义为「湿淋淋的」

definition_zh: 明亮地；鲜艳地
definition_en: in a way that gives a lot of light
core_image: 整排灯泡一起亮起
scene: 整排灯泡一下子亮了起来。 The lamps shone brightly along the street.
sceneCN: 这里 brightly 是「明亮地」（第 1 个义项：发出很多光）；句意是街上的灯整排亮起。

senses.title: With much light
senses.definition: in a way that gives a lot of light
senses.definitionCN: 以发出很多光的方式
senses.example: The lamps shone brightly along the street.
senses.exampleCN: 街上的灯整排亮起。
senses.why: This is the adverb from bright.
senses.whyCN: 这是由 bright 构成的副词。

senses.title: In strong colours
senses.definition: using strong clear colours
senses.definitionCN: 使用浓烈清晰的颜色
senses.example: The stalls were brightly painted.
senses.exampleCN: 摊位被漆得色彩鲜艳。
senses.why: Colour brightness was described as light.
senses.whyCN: 颜色的鲜明被用光来形容。

intro.en: Brightly is formed in English from bright plus -ly.
intro.cn: brightly 由 bright 加 -ly 在英语内部构成。

items.en: beorhte described a shining manner.
items.cn: beorhte 形容闪耀的样子。

items.en: brightly meant with much light.
items.cn: brightly 指带着很多光。

items.en: brightly described strong colours.
items.cn: brightly 形容鲜艳的颜色。

items.en: brightly described a happy manner.
items.cn: brightly 形容愉快的举止。

items.en: brightly covers light, colour and cheer.
items.cn: 如今 brightly 兼指光、颜色与欢快。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the br- or -ly shape; the near-meaning group gives other bright adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组共用 br- 或 -ly 的外形；近义组是其他表示明亮的副词。

entries.definition: in a brave way
in few words
a little
in strong clear colours
with a bright glow
in a way that is easy to see

normalIntro.en: Brightly adds -ly to bright, so it tells how something shines or is painted.
normalIntro.cn: brightly 由 bright 加 -ly，用来说明发光或上色的方式。

normal.en: The stars shone brightly.
normal.cn: 星星明亮地闪耀。

normal.en: The hall was brightly lit.
normal.cn: 大厅灯火通明。

normal.en: The door was brightly painted.
normal.cn: 门被漆得色彩鲜艳。

normal.en: Brightly is an adverb.
normal.cn: brightly 是副词。

normal.en: The adjective drops -ly.
normal.cn: 形容词形式去掉 -ly。

abstract.en: See a whole street of lamps at once.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街的灯一起亮起。

abstract.en: See a stall painted in red and yellow.

definition_zh: 前景；展望；观点；看法；景色；视野
definition_en: the way a situation is likely to develop, a person's settled attitude towards life or a subject, or the view seen from a particular place
core_image: 站在窗前向外望，远处的地平线和压低的云一起收进眼里
scene: 清晨的田埂上，老人蹲下去捏了一把土，又抬头看天边压着的云。 The outlook for the harvest is poor this year.
sceneCN: 这里的 outlook 是「前景、展望」（第 1 个义项：事情可能的发展方向）；句意为今年收成的前景不佳。图中可辨识物件：田埂、捏碎的土块、天边的云。

derivatives.zh: 由 look 与 out 换序构成的复合词，义为「瞭望台；守望」
由 over（在上方）与 look 复合而成，义为「俯瞰；忽视」
由 on 与 look 加表示「做某事的人」的 -er 构成，义为「旁观者」

senses.title: The likely future of a situation
senses.definition: the way a situation is likely to develop, especially in business, farming or public affairs
senses.definitionCN: 事情可能的发展方向，尤用于商业、农业或公共事务
senses.example: The outlook for the harvest is poor this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年收成的前景不佳。
senses.why: Outlook is out plus look: the word first named a place to watch from, and what a watcher could see ahead turned into the future that is coming towards everyone.
senses.whyCN: outlook 是 out 加 look：这个词最初指一个可以向外张望的位置，而守望者能望见的前方，就变成了正在朝所有人走来的未来。

senses.title: A settled way of thinking about life
senses.definition: a person's general attitude to life, or to a particular subject such as work or money
senses.definitionCN: 一个人对生活或某个话题（如工作、金钱）的总体态度
senses.example: She has a cheerful outlook on life.
senses.exampleCN: 她对生活抱着乐观的态度。
senses.why: The direction in which someone looks decides what that person notices, so the same noun moves from the eye to the mind and names a habitual point of view.
senses.whyCN: 一个人朝哪个方向看，决定了他会注意到什么，于是这个名词从眼睛转到心里，用来指一种习惯性的看法。

senses.title: The view seen from a place
senses.definition: what can be seen from a particular place, especially open country, a bay or a hillside
senses.definitionCN: 从某处望出去所能看到的景物，尤指开阔的田野、海湾或山坡
senses.example: The room has a wide outlook over the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 这个房间能望见开阔的海湾景色。
senses.why: Long before the word had anything to do with the future, it named the act of looking out and the scene that rewarded it, and that concrete sense still survives in descriptions of rooms and hills.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词和未来扯上关系之前很久，它先指「向外张望」这个动作以及由此看到的景象，这一具体义项仍活在描写房间与山丘的说法里。

intro.en: Outlook is a compound of two Old English words, out and look, recorded as a noun in the seventeenth century; it moved from a watching place to a view, and then to the future and to a state of mind.
intro.cn: outlook 由 out 与 look 两个古英语词复合而成，十七世纪才有名词记录；它从「守望之处」转到「眼前之景」，再转到「未来的走向」与「心里的态度」。

items.en: Lōcian meant to look or to see, and it is the direct ancestor of the modern verb look.
items.cn: lōcian 意为看、望，是现代动词 look 的直接祖先。

items.en: Ūt meant out or outward, and it joined verbs and nouns to show movement away from the inside.
items.cn: ūt 意为向外、朝外，常与动词和名词结合，表示由内向外。

items.en: The earliest noun outlook named a place or a post from which someone kept watch, and the act of watching from it.
items.cn: 最早的名词 outlook 指供人守望的位置或岗位，也指在那里张望这件事。

items.en: From what one sees at a watching place, the word widened to a view of land or sea, and then to the prospects that lie ahead.
items.cn: 从在守望处所见之物出发，词义先扩展到眼前的陆地或海面之景，再扩展到前方等待的种种可能。

items.en: Modern English keeps the landscape sense and adds the future sense, the likely course of events, and the mental sense, a settled way of looking at life.
items.cn: 现代英语保留风景义，又加上未来义（事情可能的走向）与精神义（看待生活的固定态度）。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words built on look or spelled close to it; the near-meaning group collects words for prospects, angles of thought and visible views.
note.cn: 形近组收由 look 构成或拼写相近的词；近义组收表示前景、思考角度与眼前景色的词。

normalIntro.en: Outlook is two Old English words joined, so the hooks keep the picture of eyes turned outward and what they meet at the far end.
normalIntro.cn: outlook 是两个古英语词的结合，所以记忆钩子始终保留「目光朝外转、在远处遇到什么」的画面。

normal.en: Outlook is simply out plus look, so the spelling itself shows the direction the eyes are turned.
normal.cn: outlook 就是 out 加 look，拼写本身已经标出目光朝向哪边。

normal.en: The watching-place sense came first, which is why a hilltop hotel can still advertise its outlook over the bay.
normal.cn: 守望之处的意思最先出现，所以山顶旅馆至今仍用这个词来宣传它望向海湾的景致。

normal.en: The weather outlook on the evening news borrows the same word for what the sky is likely to do next.
normal.cn: 晚间新闻里的天气展望也借用这个词，指天色接下来可能的走向。

normal.en: An outlook on life is not scenery but the direction a mind keeps looking in, which is why the phrase sounds slightly more settled than opinion.
normal.cn: an outlook on life 说的不是风景，而是一个头脑长期望去的方向，所以这个说法比 opinion 更显得稳固。

normal.en: Lookout reverses the two parts and keeps the same watching, so the pair is easy to confuse in reading.
normal.cn: lookout 把两部分调了个个儿，守望的意思没变，所以阅读时这一对很容易看混。

abstract.en: A word for the direction of a gaze suggests that a person's future is partly a matter of where that person chooses to look.
abstract.cn: 一个表示目光方向的词说明：一个人的未来，有一部分取决于他选择往哪里看。

abstract.en: Prospects are shared and measurable, while an outlook belongs to one mind and can be changed without anything outside changing.
abstract.cn: 前景是共享的、可以衡量的，而心态属于某一个头脑，外部什么都没变，它也可能已经变了。

abstract.en: Every window frames a view, and every view quietly tells the viewer what to expect next.
abstract.cn: 每一扇窗都框住一片景，而每一片景都在悄悄告诉看的人接下来会怎样。

definition_zh: 预订；保留；保留意见
definition_en: an arrangement to keep a seat or room, or a doubt held back
core_image: 桌上放着一张小牌子：此位已留
scene: 她提前一周订了靠窗的位子，准备给母亲过生日。 She made a reservation for a window table a week in advance for her mother's birthday.
sceneCN: 这里 reservation 是「预订」（第 1 个义项：预先保留座位或房间）；句意：她提前一周订了靠窗的位子，准备给母亲过生日。

senses.title: An arrangement to keep a place
senses.definition: an arrangement by which a seat, room, or table is kept for you
senses.definitionCN: 为你保留座位、房间或餐桌的安排
senses.example: I made a reservation for two at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 我订了七点两个人的位子。
senses.why: The noun names the result of reserving something in advance.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指预先保留某物的结果。

senses.title: Land kept for a purpose
senses.definition: an area of land kept for a particular use, such as wildlife
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途保留的一片土地，如野生动物保护
senses.example: The lake lies inside a wildlife reservation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个湖位于一片野生动物保护区内。
senses.why: Keeping something back applies to land as well as to seats.
senses.whyCN: 「保留下来」既适用于座位，也适用于土地。

senses.title: A doubt held back
senses.definition: a doubt or condition that stops you from fully agreeing
senses.definitionCN: 使你无法完全同意的疑虑或条件
senses.example: She agreed to the plan without reservation.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫无保留地同意了这个计划。
senses.why: A reservation is something kept back in the mind rather than spoken at once.
senses.whyCN: 保留意见是留在心里、没有立刻说出的东西。

intro.en: Reservation comes from Latin reservare, to keep back, from re- and servare, to keep.
intro.cn: reservation 来自拉丁语 reservare（保留），由 re- 与 servare（保存）构成。

items.en: Servare means to keep or preserve.
items.cn: servare 意为保存、保全。

items.en: Reservare means to keep back for later.
items.cn: reservare 意为留到以后。

items.en: Reserver means to reserve or hold back.
items.cn: reserver 意为保留、扣下。

items.en: Middle English reserven means to keep something back.
items.cn: 中古英语 reserven 意为把某物留下。

items.en: Reservation appears as a noun for something kept back.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪，reservation 作为名词出现，指被保留之物。

items.en: Modern English adds the senses of booking and protected land.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「预订」与「保留地」两个义项。

note.en: Reservation is the -ation noun of reserve, and it sits near its family and near words for booking and doubt.
note.cn: reservation 是 reserve 的 -ation 名词，与自身词族以及表示预订和疑虑的词相邻。

kept for later, or quiet and restrained
a member of a military reserve force

normalIntro.en: Reservation is reserve plus -ation, so it names the act of keeping something back.

normal.en: A table reservation keeps a place for you.
normal.cn: table reservation 为你留住一个位子。

normal.en: Without reservation means with no doubt held back.

normal.en: The same noun can mean a protected area kept for a purpose.

normal.en: Reserve is the verb, and reservation is the arrangement.
normal.cn: reserve 是动词，reservation 是安排。

normal.en: Compare booking: booking is the everyday word, while reservation is more formal.
normal.cn: 对比 booking：booking 更日常，reservation 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a small card on a table saying the seat is held.

abstract.en: Imagine a hand hovering over a question rather than agreeing at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手悬在问题上，没有立刻答应。

abstract.en: Think of a fenced field set aside for animals.
abstract.cn: 想象一片围起来的田地，专门留给动物。

examples.en: I made a reservation for two at seven.
examples.cn: 我订了七点两个人的位子。

examples.en: The hotel lost our reservation.

root: 拉丁语 servare（保存）→ reservare（保留）→ 古法语 reserver → 中古英语 reserven → reserve ＋ -ation → reservation。

sensesIntro.en: The noun starts as something kept back, then names a booked place, a protected area, and finally a doubt kept back in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名词从「被保留之物」开始，进而指预订的位子、受保护的区域，最后指留在心里的疑虑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a place or thing marked as held for someone.
core.cn: 核心意象：某处或某物被标记为「已为某人留住」。

branches.en: A booking is the everyday modern sense.
branches.cn: 预订，是现代日常义项。

branches.en: Protected land is something kept back for a purpose.
branches.cn: 保护区是为特定目的保留的土地。

branches.en: A doubt is something kept back from full agreement.
branches.cn: 保留意见是从完全同意中收回的部分。

branches.en: A seat and a field are both held for future use.
branches.cn: 座位与土地都是留作以后使用。

branches.en: Booking a place and withholding judgment both involve holding back.
branches.cn: 预订位子与保留判断都涉及「留住」。

intro.en: Reservation is an English -ation noun built on the Latin verb reservare.
intro.cn: reservation 是建立在拉丁动词 reservare 上的英语 -ation 名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare means to keep, and reservare means to keep back; French reserver carries the verb onward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 servare 意为保存，reservare 意为保留；法语 reserver 把这个动词继续传递。

items.example: Re- adds the idea of keeping back.
items.exampleCN: re- 增添「留在后面」的意思。

items.example: Reservare joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: reservare 把前缀与词根结合。

items.example: Reserver carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: reserver 把这个动词带入法语。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的词尾

definition_zh: 憎恨；仇恨；憎恶
definition_en: a very strong and lasting feeling of hate
core_image: 一道多年没有合上的旧伤口
scene: 多年的仇恨让他无法原谅。 Years of hatred kept him from forgiving.
sceneCN: 这里 hatred 是「仇恨」（第 1 个义项）；句意：多年的仇恨让他无法原谅。

senses.title: Deep personal hate
senses.definition: a very strong dislike that lasts a long time
senses.definitionCN: 持续很久的强烈厌恶
senses.example: Years of hatred kept him from forgiving.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的仇恨让他无法原谅。
senses.why: This is the core sense of lasting hate.
senses.whyCN: 这是持久恨意的核心义项。

senses.title: Hate between groups
senses.definition: hostile feeling between different groups of people
senses.definitionCN: 不同人群之间的敌意
senses.example: The speech spread hatred between the two groups.
senses.exampleCN: 那番话在两个群体之间散布仇恨。
senses.why: The feeling spreads from persons to groups.
senses.whyCN: 这种情绪从个人扩散到群体。

senses.title: Intense dislike of a thing
senses.definition: an intense dislike of something such as waste or lies
senses.definitionCN: 对浪费、谎言等事物的极度反感
senses.example: She has a hatred of waste.
senses.exampleCN: 她痛恨浪费。
senses.why: Hatred can fasten on habits and things.
senses.whyCN: 憎恨也能牢牢附着在习惯与事物上。

intro.en: Hatred joins the verb hate with an old suffix for a state.
intro.cn: hatred 由动词 hate 与表示状态的古后缀组合而成。

items.en: Hate came from hatian, to hate.
items.cn: hate 来自 hatian，意为憎恨。

items.en: The suffix ræden meant a condition.
items.cn: 后缀 ræden 表示状态。

items.en: Hate and the suffix shrank into hatred.
items.cn: hate 与后缀缩合成 hatred。

items.en: Hatred grew stronger than the simple verb.
items.cn: hatred 的语气比单纯动词更重。

items.en: Hatred also named hostility between groups.
items.cn: hatred 也指群体间的敌意。

note.en: Hatred is compared with look-alike words and with words for hostility.
note.cn: 把 hatred 与形近词以及表示敌意的词作比较。

entries.definition: a person who hates
wearing a hat
not wearing a hat
strong dislike
unfriendly feeling
great disgust

normalIntro.en: Hatred is hate that has settled in and stayed.
normalIntro.cn: hatred 是沉淀下来、久久不散的恨。

normal.en: Hatred grew between the two families.
normal.cn: 两个家族之间积起了仇恨。

normal.en: She spoke of him with hatred.
normal.cn: 她提起他时满怀恨意。

normal.en: Hatred blinded him to reason.
normal.cn: 仇恨让他看不见道理。

normal.en: The group spread hatred online.
normal.cn: 那个团体在网上散布仇恨。

normal.en: Time softened their hatred.
normal.cn: 时间淡化了他们的仇恨。

abstract.en: Hatred is a debt that no one can pay.
abstract.cn: 仇恨是一笔无人能还的债。

abstract.en: Hatred keeps the past alive at the cost of the present.
abstract.cn: 仇恨让过去活着，却牺牲了现在。

abstract.en: Where hatred ends, room appears.
abstract.cn: 仇恨止处，空间自现。

examples.en: Years of hatred kept him from forgiving.
examples.cn: 多年的仇恨让他无法原谅。

examples.en: The speech spread hatred between the two groups.
examples.cn: 那番话在两个群体之间散布仇恨。

examples.en: She has a hatred of waste.
examples.cn: 她痛恨浪费。

dict_mnemonic.text: hatred 由 hate 加后缀构成，指持续的恨意；deep hatred 是深仇，racial hatred 是种族仇恨，语气比动词 hate 更重。

root: 由动词 hate 加古英语后缀 ræden（状态、境况）缩合而成，字面就是「憎恨的状态」；语气比 hate 更沉重，多指持久的恨意。

sensesIntro.en: Hatred is a deep and lasting feeling of hate.
sensesIntro.cn: hatred 是深沉而持久的恨意。

core.en: Hate that has hardened over time.
core.cn: 随时间硬化下来的恨。

branches.en: Years of hatred kept him from forgiving.
branches.cn: 多年的仇恨让他无法原谅。

branches.en: The speech spread hatred between groups.
branches.cn: 那番话在群体之间散布仇恨。

branches.en: She has a hatred of waste.
branches.cn: 她痛恨浪费。

branches.en: Personal hatred can feed group conflict.
branches.cn: 个人的仇恨会助长群体冲突。

branches.en: Hatred of a group and of a habit share one heat.
branches.cn: 对群体的恨与对习惯的恨，燃烧着同一种热度。

intro.en: Hatred builds on hate and takes a plural for kinds of hate.
intro.cn: hatred 以 hate 为基础，并可用复数表示种种仇恨。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: A hater of waste, she saved everything.
items.exampleCN: 她痛恨浪费，什么都留着。
可恨的话语会伤人多年。

items.example: He spoke hatefully of his rival.

items.exampleCN: 那条招人恨的规定被废除了。

definition_zh: 本科生；大学生；（作定语）本科的
definition_en: a student at a university who has not yet taken a first degree
core_image: 阶梯上还没拿到第一块牌子的那个年轻人
scene: 九月开学，图书馆门前排着长队，手里拿着新学生证的都是刚入学的年轻人。 She was still an undergraduate when she wrote her first book.
sceneCN: 这里 undergraduate 是「本科生」（第 1 个义项：尚未取得学位的大学生）；句意为她写第一本书时还是本科生。还没拿到第一块牌子的年轻人，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：本科的；大学生的

derivatives.zh: 去掉前缀的原词，义为「毕业生；研究生」
口语缩略形式，义为「本科生」
复合形容词，义为「本科层次的」

senses.title: A student without a first degree
senses.definition: a student working toward a bachelor’s degree
senses.definitionCN: 正在攻读学士学位的学生
senses.example: The lab takes two undergraduates each summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这个实验室每年夏天招收两名本科生。
senses.why: Graduare in Latin means to take a step, and gradus is a step; under marks the stage below the degree step.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 graduare 意为迈一步，gradus 是台阶；under 标记学位那一级之下的阶段。

senses.title: A student at a college in the first cycle
senses.definition: a person at college in their first course of higher study
senses.definitionCN: 在大学第一级课程中就读的人
senses.example: Undergraduates here live in colleges, not flats.
senses.exampleCN: 这里的大学生住在学院里，而不在校外公寓。
senses.why: British universities above all use the word to separate students from postgraduates on the same campus.
senses.whyCN: 尤以英国大学如此，用这个词把同一校园里的本科生与研究生区分开。

senses.title: Study at the first level
senses.definition: used before nouns for courses and degrees below master’s level
senses.definitionCN: 用于硕士水平以下的课程与学位名词之前
senses.example: She teaches an undergraduate seminar on poetry.
senses.exampleCN: 她教一门本科诗歌研讨课。
senses.why: The noun freely becomes a label for the whole level of study.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词又自由地转作整个学习阶段的标签。

senses.title: A part that is still in progress
senses.titleCN: 尚未完成本科阶段的人
senses.definition: a person whose degree is not yet awarded and so not yet a graduate
senses.definitionCN: 学位尚未授予、因而还不算 graduate 的人
senses.example: He is an undergraduate until the results come out.
senses.exampleCN: 成绩公布之前他还算本科生。
senses.why: The prefix is a status marker: the step has not been taken yet.
senses.whyCN: 前缀是个身份标记：那一步还没有迈出去。

senses.title: A young member of a learned community
senses.definition: in older usage, a beginning student within a college
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法中指学院里刚开始学习的人
senses.example: In 1820 the college had forty undergraduates.
senses.exampleCN: 1820 年这所学院有四十名在读学生。
senses.why: In that older world the word simply placed a beginner at the foot of the college ladder.
senses.whyCN: 在那个更早的世界里，这个词只是把一个初学者放在学院梯子的最下一级。

intro.en: The word is a Latin step, with an English prefix marking the stage below it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语的「一步」，加英语前缀标记那一步之下的阶段。

items.en: Gradus means a step or a degree, and gradus honoris is an academic degree.
items.cn: gradus 意为台阶或等级，gradus honoris 即学位。

items.en: Graduare means to take a degree, and the medieval university is its stage.
items.cn: graduare 意为取得学位，其舞台就是中世纪大学。

items.en: The noun graduate enters English from that academic sense.
items.cn: graduate 由这层学术义进入英语。

items.en: Undergraduate is formed with the prefix to name students below the degree step.
items.cn: 加上前缀构成 undergraduate，指位于学位台阶之下的学生。

items.en: The Oxford and Cambridge systems fix the British usage in the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 十九世纪牛津与剑桥的制度把英式用法固定下来。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the grad- stem of steps and degrees, and the near-meaning group names student roles.
note.cn: 形近组共用表示台阶与学位的 grad- 词干，近义组列出学生身份。

entries.definition: a person who has a degree
the ceremony of taking a degree
a step on a scale
a student beyond a first degree
a person who studies
a first-year student
a student in the final year

normalIntro.en: Gradus is a step, so an undergraduate has not yet stepped onto the degree level.
normalIntro.cn: gradus 是台阶，undergraduate 就是还没踏上学位那一级的人。

normal.en: Graduate means the step has been taken, and undergraduate means it has not.
normal.cn: graduate 表示已迈上那一步，undergraduate 表示还没迈上。

normal.en: Grade and gradual come from the same step, one a rank, one a pace.
normal.cn: grade 与 gradual 同出这一步，一个是等级，一个是步伐。

normal.en: In British use undergraduates are at college, while postgraduates remain after the degree.
normal.cn: 英式用法里本科生在学院读书，postgraduate 是拿过学位后继续读的人。

normal.en: Undergrad is the joking short form heard on campus.
normal.cn: 校园里常听到打趣的缩略说法 undergrad。

normal.en: The plural undergraduates is regular, with no change of the stem.
normal.cn: 复数 undergraduates 规则变化，词干不变。

abstract.en: See a staircase with the degree marked one step higher.
abstract.cn: 看见一段楼梯，学位那一级标得更高一点。

abstract.en: Watch a young person standing one step below it with books.
abstract.cn: 看一个年轻人抱着书站在它下面一级。

abstract.en: Notice that the sign on that step never names the person, only the gap.
abstract.cn: 注意那一级上的标牌并不叫出人名，只标出这段差距。

examples.en: Most undergraduates live on campus in their first year.
examples.cn: 大多数本科生第一年住在校内。

examples.en: He completed an undergraduate degree in economics.
examples.cn: 他修完了经济学本科学位。

examples.en: The journal is written for undergraduates, not specialists.
examples.cn: 这份刊物是给本科生而不是专家看的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安得瓜爵特」——还没安得上学位这顶「爵」帽，所以只能叫本科生。

root: under-（在……之下）+ graduate（拉丁语 gradus「台阶、等级」→ graduare「取得学位」）；同族有 grade、graduation、postgraduate

sensesIntro.en: The word marks a place on a staircase: below the step where a degree is taken.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词标记楼梯上的位置：在授予学位那一级之下。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a young person standing one step below the degree.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个年轻人站在学位那一级的下方。

branches.en: The person branch: the student working toward a degree.
branches.cn: 人分支：正在攻读学位的学生。

branches.en: The labelling branch: courses, degrees, and journals.
branches.cn: 标签分支：课程、学位与刊物。

branches.en: The status branch: not yet counted among graduates.
branches.cn: 身份分支：还不在毕业生之列。

branches.en: The older branch: a beginning member of a college.
branches.cn: 旧义分支：学院里初入门的人。

branches.en: The plain campus sense heard every September.
branches.cn: 每年九月都能听到的校园义。

intro.en: An English prefix on a Latin word for a step.
intro.cn: 英语前缀加在表示「台阶」的拉丁词上。

latinIntro.en: The grad- root of steps also gives grade, gradual, and progress.
latinIntro.cn: 表示台阶的 grad- 词根还生出 grade、gradual、progress。

items.example: Under- marks the stage below a degree.
items.exampleCN: under- 标记学位之下的一级。

items.example: Graduare means to take a degree.
Undergraduate names the person at that stage.
items.exampleCN: undergraduate 指处于该阶段的人。

definition_zh: 专攻；专门从事；使专业化
definition_en: to focus on one subject or kind of work, or to make something more focused
core_image: 一位年轻医生把所有时间都投入心脏研究，桌上只摆着这一科的书籍
scene: 她专攻儿童医学。 She specializes in children's medicine.
sceneCN: 这里 specialize 是「专攻」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她专攻儿童医学。

senses.title: To focus on a subject
senses.definition: to study or work on one subject in depth
senses.definitionCN: 深入学习或研究某一门学科
senses.example: She specializes in children's medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 她专攻儿童医学。
senses.why: This is the core modern sense of narrowing study.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代表示收窄研究范围的核心含义。

senses.title: To work in one line
senses.definition: to do one particular kind of business or work
senses.definitionCN: 从事某一特定种类的业务或工作
senses.example: The firm specializes in small hotels.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司专门经营小型旅馆。
senses.why: Businesses specialize by limiting what they offer.
senses.whyCN: 企业通过限定所提供的服务来实现专门化。

senses.title: To become focused
senses.definition: to develop into separate, more focused fields
senses.definitionCN: 发展为各自更专门的分支领域
senses.example: Medicine has specialized into many branches.
senses.exampleCN: 医学已分化为许多专门分支。
senses.why: A whole field can specialize, not only a person.
senses.whyCN: 不只是个人，整个领域也可以走向专门化。

intro.en: Specialize was built from Latin specialis to name the act of narrowing to one field.
intro.cn: specialize 由拉丁语 specialis 构成，用来表示收窄到某一领域的行为。

items.en: Specialis meant of a particular kind.
items.cn: specialis 意为属于某一特定种类的。

items.en: Spécialiser named the act of making something specific.
items.cn: spécialiser 指使某物变得专门的行为。

items.en: Specialize entered English as a verb of focused study.
items.cn: specialize 作为表示专注研究的动词进入英语。

items.en: To specialize in a trade meant to make it one's whole work.
items.cn: specialize in a trade 表示把它当作全部工作。

items.en: Whole industries came to be described as specialized.
items.cn: 整个行业也开始被形容为专业化的。

note.en: Specialize is compared with look-alike words and verbs of focusing.
note.cn: 把 specialize 与形近词以及表示聚焦的动词作比较。

entries.definition: unusual or dedicated
a special skill or dish
an expert
to give attention to one thing
to give all effort to one thing
to study a main subject

normalIntro.en: To specialize is to choose one field and give it all your hours.
normalIntro.cn: specialize 就是选定一个领域，把时间全交给它。

normal.en: She specializes in children's medicine.
normal.cn: 她专攻儿童医学。

normal.en: The firm specializes in small hotels.
normal.cn: 这家公司专门经营小型旅馆。

normal.en: Medicine has specialized into many branches.
normal.cn: 医学已分化为许多专门分支。

normal.en: He specializes in repairing old clocks.
normal.cn: 他专门修理旧钟表。

normal.en: The team uses highly specialized equipment.
normal.cn: 团队使用高度专业化的设备。

abstract.en: To specialize is to say no to a thousand fields.
abstract.cn: 专攻，就是对千百个领域说不。

abstract.en: Depth is bought with the coin of breadth.
abstract.cn: 深度是用广度这枚硬币买来的。

abstract.en: A river narrows before it runs deep.
abstract.cn: 河流先收窄，才能流得深。

examples.en: She specializes in children's medicine.
examples.cn: 她专攻儿童医学。

examples.en: The firm specializes in small hotels.
examples.cn: 这家公司专门经营小型旅馆。

examples.en: Medicine has specialized into many branches.
examples.cn: 医学已分化为许多专门分支。

dict_mnemonic.text: specialize 由 special 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，表示「使专门化、专攻」；specialize in 是「专攻某一领域」，specialized 是「专业化的」，specialist 是「专家」，specialization 是「专业化」。

root: 由拉丁语 specialis（特定种类的）加动词后缀 -ize 构成，核心义为使某事物限定在某一特定领域，即专攻、专门化。

sensesIntro.en: Specialize means to focus study on one subject, to work in one line, or to become more narrowly focused.
sensesIntro.cn: specialize 指把学习集中在一门学科、专门从事某一行业，或变得更为专门化。

core.en: Narrowing attention to one field.
core.cn: 把注意力收窄到一个领域。

branches.en: A student reads only books on the heart.
branches.cn: 一名学生只读关于心脏的书。

branches.en: A small firm takes only one kind of client.
branches.cn: 一家小公司只接一类客户。

branches.en: One old science splits into many new ones.
branches.cn: 一门古老的学科分裂成许多新学科。

branches.en: Study and trade both narrow to gain depth.
branches.cn: 学问与生意都靠收窄来获得深度。

branches.en: A person and a whole field can both specialize.
branches.cn: 个人与整个领域都能走向专门化。

intro.en: Specialize forms nouns of focus and related adjectives.
intro.cn: specialize 构成表示专注的名词和相关形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is specialis, of a particular kind, from species, a kind.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁词根是 specialis（特定种类的），源于 species（种类）。

items.example: Fish soup is the house specialty.

definition_zh: 过敏的；对……过敏的；对……极反感的
definition_en: having a physical reaction to a substance, or strongly disliking something
core_image: 皮肤上突然浮起的红点，一碰到花粉就发痒
scene: 春天花粉飞扬，她一出门就不停打喷嚏。 She is allergic to pollen and sneezes all through spring.
sceneCN: 这里 allergic 是「过敏的」（第 1 个义项：对某物质产生身体过敏反应）；句意为她对花粉过敏，整个春天都在打喷嚏。

pos.zh: 形容词：过敏的；对……极反感的

derivatives.zh: 去掉形容词后缀得到的基础名词，义为「过敏」
由 allergy 加 -gen 构成，义为「过敏原」
由 allergy 加 -ist 构成，义为「过敏科医生」
由 allergen 加 -ic 构成，义为「引起过敏的」

senses.title: Reacting physically to a substance
senses.definition: having an immune reaction such as sneezing, itching, or swelling after contact with a particular substance
senses.definitionCN: 接触某种特定物质后出现打喷嚏、发痒或肿胀等免疫反应
senses.example: My brother is allergic to peanuts.
senses.exampleCN: 我弟弟对花生过敏。
senses.why: Greek allos meant other and ergon meant work; allergy named the body working against an otherwise harmless other thing.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 allos 意为「别的」，ergon 意为「工作」；allergy 命名身体对一种本来无害的「他者」发起抵抗工作。

senses.title: Strongly disliking something
senses.definition: strongly averse to something, often in a humorous or emphatic way
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物强烈反感，常带幽默或强调语气
senses.example: He is allergic to meetings that last all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他对开一下午的会深恶痛绝。
senses.why: The body's rejection of a substance becomes a metaphor for the mind's rejection of an idea, and the reaction is equally automatic.
senses.whyCN: 身体对物质的排斥，被借喻为头脑对观念的排斥，而且反应同样自动。

senses.title: Caused by allergy
senses.definition: describing a disease or symptom produced by an allergic reaction
senses.definitionCN: 形容由过敏反应引起的疾病或症状
senses.example: The clinic treats children with allergic asthma.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所治疗患过敏性哮喘的儿童。
senses.why: In medical compounds the word marks cause rather than the sufferer: the asthma is not allergic, it is asthma caused by allergy.
senses.whyCN: 在医学复合词里，这个词标的是病因而不是患者：哮喘本身不过敏，而是由过敏引起的哮喘。

intro.en: Allergic is a twentieth-century medical coinage built from two Greek words and later borrowed by everyday speech.
intro.cn: allergic 是二十世纪的医学新造词，由两个希腊词构成，后来被日常语言借用。

items.en: Greek allos meant other or different, the first half of the coinage.
items.cn: 希腊语 allos 意为「别的、不同的」，是新造词的前半部分。

items.en: Greek ergon meant work or action, and it also gives English energy and ergonomic.
items.cn: 希腊语 ergon 意为工作或作用，也是英语 energy 与 ergonomic 的来源。

items.en: The physician Clemens von Pirquet coined allergy for the body's altered, over-reactive response to a foreign substance.
items.cn: 医生克莱门斯·冯·皮尔凯造出 allergy 一词，指身体对外来物质的改变了的过度反应。

items.en: English borrowed allergy in the early twentieth century as the medical term spread.
items.cn: 二十世纪初，随着医学术语传播，英语借入了 allergy。

items.en: The adjective allergic followed, formed with the Latin-derived suffix -ic.
items.cn: 形容词 allergic 随后出现，用源自拉丁语的 -ic 构成。

items.en: Later the word was extended to strong dislike, first in speech and then in dictionaries.
items.cn: 后来这个词被扩展到强烈反感，先出现在口语，再进入词典。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the allergy family; the near-meaning group gathers words for sensitivity and intolerance.
note.cn: 形近组收 allergy 词族；近义组收表示敏感与不耐受的词。

entries.definition: The medical condition behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指形容词背后的医学状况，即过敏。

entries.definition: A substance that triggers an allergic reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 指引发过敏反应的物质，即过敏原。

entries.definition: A doctor who treats allergies.
Able to cause an allergic reaction.
entries.definitionCN: 指能够引起过敏反应的。

entries.definition: Reacting easily to a substance or situation, a broader word.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某物质或情境容易起反应，是更宽泛的词。

entries.definition: Unable to digest or accept a food or substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法消化或接受某种食物或物质。

entries.definition: Reacting more strongly than usual to a stimulus.
entries.definitionCN: 指对刺激的反应比平常更强烈。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Greek meaning other work and the visible signs of a reaction.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用希腊语「他者 + 工作」的含义，以及看得见的反应迹象。

normal.en: Allergy is other work: the body works against something that should be harmless.
normal.cn: allergy 是「他者的工作」：身体对本来无害的东西发起抵抗。

normal.en: Allergic to pollen means pollen starts that work, and the nose pays.
normal.cn: allergic to pollen 意为花粉启动这项工作，鼻子付出代价。

normal.en: Allergic reaction is the body's overreaction, not the substance's attack.
normal.cn: allergic reaction 是身体的过度反应，而不是物质的攻击。

normal.en: Allergic asthma is asthma caused by allergy, so read the compound from right to left.
normal.cn: allergic asthma 是由过敏引起的哮喘，所以要从右往左读这个复合词。

normal.en: Saying you are allergic to meetings borrows the body's automatic refusal for the mind.
normal.cn: 说自己对开会有过敏反应，是把身体的自动拒绝借给头脑使用。

abstract.en: Picture a quiet house where a harmless cat walks in, and every alarm in the walls goes off.
abstract.cn: 想象一间安静的屋子，一只无害的猫走进来，墙里所有警报同时响起。

abstract.en: Nothing in the cat changed; only the house's way of working changed.
abstract.cn: 猫没有变，变的只是屋子运作的方式。

abstract.en: Allergic is the name of that house, not the name of the cat.
abstract.cn: allergic 是那间屋子的名字，不是那只猫的名字。

examples.en: She is allergic to shellfish and carries medicine with her.
examples.cn: 她对贝类过敏，随身带着药。

examples.en: The doctor asked whether anyone in the family was allergic.
examples.cn: 医生问家里是否有人过敏。

examples.en: He is allergic to loud arguments in small rooms.
examples.cn: 他对小房间里的高声争吵极为反感。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额了叽刻」——额，一碰花粉就叽叽刻刻打喷嚏，过敏了

root: 由希腊语 allos（别的、不同的）与 ergon（工作、作用）构成；一九零六年由医生皮尔凯造出 allergy，指身体对外来物质的过度反应，再加 -ic 构成形容词。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses describe the body's reaction and the illness it causes; one extends the reaction to the mind's strong dislike.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项描述身体的反应与由此引起的疾病；一个义项把这种反应延伸到头脑的强烈反感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a harmless substance enters the body, and the body's defences treat it as an invader.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种无害物质进入身体，身体的防线却把它当作入侵者。

branches.en: THE OTHER: Greek allos marks the substance as foreign, and the body reacts to its foreignness.
branches.cn: 他者线：希腊语 allos 标出物质的外来性，身体正是对这种外来性起反应。

branches.en: THE WORK: ergon is the body's work, and allergy is that work turned against something harmless.
branches.cn: 工作线：ergon 是身体的运作，过敏就是这项运作反过来对付无害之物。

branches.en: THE DISEASE: medical compounds use the word to mark a cause, as in allergic asthma.
branches.cn: 疾病线：医学复合词用这个词标出病因，如过敏性哮喘。

branches.en: THE MIND: the body's automatic refusal becomes a metaphor for strong dislike.
branches.cn: 头脑线：身体的自动拒绝变成强烈反感的比喻。

branches.en: THE REFLEX: in both senses the reaction is fast and not chosen.
branches.cn: 反射线：无论哪个义项，反应都很快且非自愿。

intro.en: Allergic is a Greek-based medical word with a Latin-style adjective ending and a productive family around allergy.
intro.cn: allergic 是希腊词基的医学词，带拉丁式形容词词尾，并围绕 allergy 有能产词族。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek rather than Latin, so the Latin entries are limited to the adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词根来自希腊语而非拉丁语，因此拉丁条目只限形容词词尾。

items.exampleCN: 它是 allergy 的前半部分。

items.exampleCN: 它是 allergy 的后半部分。

items.meaning: the body's response to an allergen
items.example: The rash was an allergic reaction.

definition_zh: 微风；轻而易举的事；轻快地走
definition_en: a light gentle wind
core_image: 午后窗帘被风轻轻吹起
scene: 午后的窗帘被一阵微风吹起。 A breeze lifted the curtain in the afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 breeze 是「微风」（第 1 个义项：轻柔的风）；句意是午后的窗帘被微风吹起。

pos.zh: 名词：微风；轻而易举的事

senses.title: A light wind
senses.definition: a light gentle wind
senses.definitionCN: 轻柔的风
senses.example: A breeze lifted the curtain in the afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 午后的窗帘被一阵微风吹起。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from the sea air.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自海上的空气。

senses.title: An easy task
senses.definition: something very easy to do
senses.definitionCN: 做起来非常容易的事
senses.example: The test was a breeze.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考试轻而易举。
senses.why: A soft wind pictured something that takes no effort.
senses.whyCN: 轻柔的风被用来比喻毫不费力的事。

senses.title: To move quickly and lightly
senses.definition: to walk somewhere quickly and easily
senses.definitionCN: 轻松迅速地走到某处
senses.example: She breezed into the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她轻快地走进房间。
senses.why: The movement of wind became a way of walking.
senses.whyCN: 风的流动变成了走路的方式。

intro.en: Breeze came from a Spanish word for the north-east wind.
intro.cn: breeze 来自西班牙语中表示东北风的词。

items.en: briza named a cold north-east wind.
items.cn: briza 指寒冷的东北风。

items.en: English breeze named a sea wind.
items.cn: 英语 breeze 指海风。

items.en: breeze meant any light wind.
items.cn: breeze 指任何轻柔的风。

items.en: a breeze meant an easy task.
items.cn: a breeze 指轻松的事。

items.en: breeze covers wind, ease and light movement.
items.cn: 如今 breeze 兼指微风、轻松与轻快的动作。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the br- or -eeze shape; the near-meaning group gives other air words.
note.cn: 形近组共用 br- 或 -eeze 的外形；近义组是与风有关的词。

entries.definition: to become hard and cold like ice
to cook meat slowly in liquid
to look through things casually
air moving across the land
a current of air in a room
a sudden strong rush of wind

normalIntro.en: Breeze is a wind so light that it only lifts a curtain.
normalIntro.cn: breeze 是轻得只吹起窗帘的风。

normal.en: A light breeze crossed the garden.
normal.cn: 一阵微风穿过花园。

normal.en: A sea breeze cools the shore.
normal.cn: 海风让岸边凉快。

normal.en: The test was a breeze.

abstract.en: See a curtain lifting without hands.
abstract.cn: 想象窗帘没有手也飘了起来。

abstract.en: See leaves turning over softly.
abstract.cn: 想象叶子轻轻翻动。

sensesIntro.en: A soft wind, an easy task and a light way of moving.
