definition_zh: 面对；正视；对抗；使面临
definition_en: to face a difficult situation or person directly
core_image: 两个人隔着桌子对视，谁也没有移开目光
scene: 她决定不再回避，直接找对方把问题说清。 She decided to confront him about the missing money.
sceneCN: 这里 confront 指「当面质问」（第 2 个义项：直接与当事人对质）；句意是她决定就那笔失踪的钱当面质问他。

senses.title: Face a hard situation
senses.definition: to deal with a difficult problem or fact directly
senses.definitionCN: 直接处理困难的问题或事实
senses.example: We must confront the problem, not hide it.
senses.exampleCN: 我们必须正视这个问题，而不是藏起来。
senses.why: A problem faced becomes a task, while a problem avoided becomes a fear.
senses.whyCN: 问题被面对就成了任务，被躲开就成了恐惧。

senses.title: Stand up to someone
senses.definition: to meet a person face to face about a conflict
senses.definitionCN: 为了一件冲突与某人当面对质
senses.example: She confronted him about the missing money.
senses.exampleCN: 她就那笔失踪的钱当面质问他。
senses.why: A quiet complaint behind a back is weaker than one clear sentence in front.
senses.whyCN: 背后小声抱怨，比不上当面一句清楚的话。

senses.title: Put face to face with
senses.definition: to make someone have to deal with something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 使某人不得不应付困难的事
senses.example: The town is confronted with a water shortage.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇正面临缺水。
senses.why: Some difficulties arrive without invitation and must still be met.
senses.whyCN: 有些困难不请自来，却仍然必须应对。

intro.en: Confront comes from Latin confrontare, to stand face to face, from com-, together, and frons, the forehead or face.
intro.cn: confront 来自拉丁语 confrontare，意为面对面站着，由 com-（一起）与 frons（额头、脸）构成。

items.en: Frons meant the forehead and, by extension, the whole face.
items.cn: frons 意为额头，并引申为整张脸。

items.en: Confrontare meant to bring two faces into the same line of sight.
items.cn: confrontare 意为让两张脸进入同一条视线。

items.en: French confronter used the word for meeting an opponent.
items.cn: 法语 confronter 用这个词表示与对手会面。

items.en: English confront first meant to stand facing someone.
items.cn: 英语 confront 最初指面对面站着。

items.en: It now also means to face a problem or to be faced with one.
items.cn: 如今它也指面对一个问题，或被迫面临某个问题。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that begin like confront, and the meaning group names other ways of facing something hard.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 confront 词形相近的词，近义组列出其他表示面对困难的说法。

entries.definition: to admit that you did something wrong
to make someone unable to think clearly
to keep within limits
to deal with something difficult
to question or oppose someone bravely
to make a serious effort to deal with a problem

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from two faces across a table, then move to a hard problem and to a town short of water.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从桌子两边对视的脸开始，再走到棘手的问题与缺水的城镇。

normal.en: Con- is together and front is the face, so confront is to put faces together.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，front 是脸面，所以 confront 就是把脸对到一处。

normal.en: To confront a problem is to sit down opposite it and look.
normal.cn: 面对问题，就是坐到它对面，然后看着它。

normal.en: A confrontation begins the moment both people stop looking away.
normal.cn: 对峙开始于两个人都不再移开目光的那一刻。

normal.en: Be confronted with bad news and you still choose what to do next.
normal.cn: 被迫面对坏消息时，你仍然可以选择下一步。

normal.en: The front of a building faces the street, and a brave person faces the truth.
normal.cn: 建筑的正面朝向街道，勇敢的人则朝向真相。

abstract.en: Picture two chairs placed exactly opposite each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子正对着摆好。

abstract.en: Picture a locked door you finally push open.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇你终于推开的锁着的门。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of water rising in front of a town.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵水墙在小镇前升起。

examples.en: The country must confront its water crisis.
examples.cn: 这个国家必须正视自己的水危机。

examples.en: He confronted his friend about the broken promise.
examples.cn: 他就那个没守住的承诺当面质问朋友。

examples.en: We were confronted with a difficult choice.
examples.cn: 我们面临一个艰难的选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 confront 记成 con（一起）加 front（正面）：两张脸正面相对，就是面对；面对面提出异议，就是当面质问。

root: 源自拉丁语 confrontare（com 一起 + frons 额头、脸），本义是面对面站着，后引申为面对、对抗与使面临。

sensesIntro.en: From two faces meeting across a table, to meeting a problem, and finally to being pushed into a difficulty.
sensesIntro.cn: 从桌边两张相对的脸，到与问题正面相遇，最后到被推进困境之中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two faces at one table, neither turning aside.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一张桌边的两张脸，谁都不转向别处。

branches.en: Facing a problem is the first act of solving it.
branches.cn: 正视问题，是解决问题的第一个动作。

branches.en: Confronting a person turns a private worry into an open conversation.
branches.cn: 当面质问某人，把私下的担忧变成公开的对话。

branches.en: Being confronted with something leaves no room to look away.
branches.cn: 被迫面临某事时，就再没有转开视线的余地。

branches.en: Both senses pull a hidden matter into the open.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把藏着的事拉到明处。

branches.en: A person can confront another, and a situation can confront us.
branches.cn: 人可以质问另一个人，处境也会反过来逼到我们面前。

intro.en: Confront is built on Latin com-, together, plus frons, the face or forehead.
intro.cn: confront 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 frons（脸、额头）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin face base front- also appears in front, frontal and affront.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的脸面词基 front- 也出现在 front、frontal 与 affront 中。

items.example: Every winter the town confronts deep snow.
items.exampleCN: 每年冬天这个镇都要面对大雪。

items.example: He sat confronting his own fear.
items.exampleCN: 他坐着面对自己的恐惧。

items.example: The talk ended in a confrontation.
items.exampleCN: 这次谈话以一场对峙收场。

items.example: The front of the house faces south.
The remark affronted the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 这句话冒犯了整个团队。

definition_zh: 把……分类；把……归入某类；把（文件）列为机密
definition_en: to arrange things into groups by shared features, or to declare official information secret
core_image: 长桌上摊开的标本被一一放进贴标签的盒子
scene: 管理员把新到的化石摊在长桌上。 Scientists classify these shells by shape and age.
sceneCN: 这里 classify 指「把……分类」（第 1 个义项：按共同特征把事物归入各组）；句意是科学家按形状与年代给这些贝壳分类。

senses.title: To sort into groups
senses.definition: to put things into groups according to features they share
senses.definitionCN: 按共同特征把事物放进各组
senses.example: The students classified the leaves by shape.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们按形状给叶子分类。
senses.why: The verb joins the Latin word for a division with the verb to make, so it means to make divisions.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把拉丁语表示划分的词与表示做的动词结合，意为造出划分。

senses.title: To mark information secret
senses.definition: to give official papers a security level that limits who may read them
senses.definitionCN: 给官方文件定下保密等级，限制可阅读的人
senses.example: The report was classified for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告被列为机密三十年。
senses.why: A secret file is placed in a restricted class, so the sorting verb took on this official sense.
senses.whyCN: 机密文件被归入受限的等级，于是这个分类动词带上了官方含义。

intro.en: Classify is a learned compound of the Latin words for a division and for making.
intro.cn: classify 是拉丁语表示划分与表示做的两个词构成的学术复合词。

items.en: Classis meant a division or a class.
items.cn: classis 意为划分或等级。

items.en: Facere meant to make or to do.
items.cn: facere 意为制作或做。

items.en: Classifier named the work of sorting plants and minerals.
items.cn: classifier 指给植物与矿物分类的工作。

items.en: English took classify from the French naturalists.
items.cn: 英语从法国博物学家那里借入 classify。

items.en: The verb also came to mean restricting official papers.
items.cn: 这个动词后来又表示限制官方文件的阅读。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that differ by one or two letters, while the meaning group names sorting actions.
note.cn: 形近组列出只差一两个字母的词，近义组列出分类动作。

entries.definition: to make something easier to understand
a group or a lesson
a person or device that sorts things
entries.definitionCN: 给事物分类的人或装置

entries.definition: to put things in order by type
to place something in a named group
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放进有名称的组

entries.definition: to put things in a planned order

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the class root, the -ify ending and the two very different senses.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用 class 词根、-ify 后缀以及两个差别很大的义项。

normal.en: Classify is class plus -ify, so it means to make classes.
normal.cn: classify 是 class 加 -ify，所以意思是造出类别。

normal.en: Classify by and classify as are the two patterns: by a feature, as a member.
normal.cn: classify by 与 classify as 是两个句型：按某特征分，归为某成员。

normal.en: A classified document has a class of secrecy, not a class of students.
normal.cn: a classified document 有保密等级，不是指学生班级。

normal.en: The noun is classification and the doer is classifier, both from the same verb.
normal.cn: 名词是 classification，执行者是 classifier，都出自这个动词。

normal.en: Scientists classify first and name later.
normal.cn: 科学家先分类，后命名。

abstract.en: Picture a long table of shells with small paper labels beside each pile.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌上摆满贝壳，每堆旁边都有小纸标签。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp folder where every page holds one kind only.
abstract.cn: 想象一本邮票册，每一页只放一个种类。

abstract.en: Picture a folder stamped with a red word and locked in a drawer.
abstract.cn: 想象一个盖了红字的文件夹被锁进抽屉。

examples.en: The students classified the leaves by shape.
examples.cn: 学生们按形状给叶子分类。

examples.en: These birds are classified as rare in the region.
examples.cn: 这些鸟在该地区被列为稀有。

examples.en: The report was classified for thirty years.
examples.cn: 这份报告被列为机密三十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 class 想成「类」，ify 想成「使」：使东西各归其类，就是分类。

root: 由拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）组合，经法语 classifier 进入英语，本义是做出分组。

sensesIntro.en: One verb sorts objects into groups and also puts secret papers into a restricted class.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个动词既把实物分进各组，也把机密文件归入受限等级。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: specimens laid out and moved into labelled boxes.
core.cn: 核心意象：标本摊开来，被逐一移进贴标签的盒子。

branches.en: The verb makes groups out of mixed things.
branches.cn: 这个动词把混杂之物分成组。

branches.en: Official papers are put into a secrecy class.
branches.cn: 官方文件被放进保密等级。

branches.en: Both senses place something inside a class.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把某物放进某一类。

branches.en: A shared feature is the knife that cuts the groups apart.
branches.cn: 共同特征是切开各组的那把刀。

branches.en: Secrecy is only one class among many.
branches.cn: 保密只是众多类别中的一类。

intro.en: The verb takes -es, -ed and -ing, and feeds the whole classification family.
intro.cn: 这个动词接 -es、-ed、-ing，并衍生出整个 classification 家族。

latinIntro.en: The base pairs Latin classis, a division, with facere, to make.
latinIntro.cn: 词基把拉丁语 classis（划分）与 facere（做）配在一起。

items.example: We classify the samples by age.
items.exampleCN: 我们按年代给样本分类。

items.meaning: the verb with a single subject
items.exampleCN: 她给每件新发现物分类。

items.example: They classified the rocks last week.
items.exampleCN: 他们上周把岩石分了类。

items.meaning: a person or device that sorts

items.exampleCN: 这块碎片几乎无法归类。

items.meaning: forming verbs that mean to make
items.meaningCN: 构成表示使之怎样的动词

latinEntries.example: Facere supplies the second half of classify.
latinEntries.exampleCN: facere 提供了 classify 的后半部分。

definition_zh: 痛苦的；悲惨的；恶劣的；破旧的；少得可怜的
definition_en: extremely unhappy or distressed; very unpleasant to experience; of very poor quality or in a bad state; and, of an amount, pitifully small
core_image: 雨里缩在破屋檐下的人，衣服湿透，肩膀一直抖
scene: 冬天的雨下了一整天，屋檐漏风，一个人裹着湿透的外套坐在台阶上，肩膀一直抖。 The refugees spent a miserable night in the leaking tent.
sceneCN: 这里是「痛苦的、悲惨的」（第 1 个义项：身心都很难受）；句意为难民们在一顶漏雨的帐篷里度过了一个悲惨的夜晚。图中可辨识物件：漏风的屋檐、湿透的外套、发抖的肩膀。

pos.zh: 痛苦的；悲惨的；恶劣的；破旧的；少得可怜的

derivatives.zh: 由 miserable 去 le 加 -ly 构成，义为「痛苦地；悲惨地」
与 miserable 同出拉丁语 miser，义为「痛苦；苦难」

senses.title: Extremely unhappy and distressed
senses.definition: feeling very unhappy, hopeless or lonely, especially over a stretch of time rather than for a moment
senses.definitionCN: 感到非常不快、无望或孤独，尤指持续一段时间而非一时
senses.example: She felt miserable after the argument and could not sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 争吵之后她心里难受，睡不着觉。
senses.why: Latin miser named a person at the bottom of fortune, so the adjective begins with an inner state rather than with the weather or the room around the person.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 miser 指一个沦落到命运底层的人，所以这个形容词的起点是人的内心状态，而不是他周围的天气或房间。

senses.title: Very unpleasant to live through or experience
senses.definition: of weather, conditions or an event, so bad that it makes people deeply uncomfortable
senses.definitionCN: 指天气、条件或事件坏到让人非常难受
senses.example: The team played on through miserable weather.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在恶劣的天气里继续比赛。
senses.why: Once the word names a wretched person, it can name the conditions that produce that wretchedness, so the cause takes the same adjective as the effect.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词能形容一个可怜人，它也就能形容造成这种可怜处境的条件，于是原因和结果共用了同一个形容词。

senses.title: Of very poor quality or in a bad state
senses.definition: of a place or thing, inadequate, shabby and depressing to be in or to use
senses.definitionCN: 指地方或物品简陋、破败，待在里面或使用它让人沮丧
senses.example: They lived in a miserable little room above a shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们住在商店楼上的一间破旧小屋。
senses.why: A dwelling that makes its occupants wretched earns the same word, so the misery of the person is transferred to the object that houses him.
senses.whyCN: 让住户痛苦的住处会得到同一个形容词，人的痛苦因此被转移到了容纳他的物件上。

senses.title: Pitifully small in amount
senses.definition: of a sum of money or an amount, so small that it seems unfair or almost insulting
senses.definitionCN: 指金额或数量小得不公平、几乎带侮辱意味
senses.example: He was paid a miserable sum for a whole week of work.
senses.exampleCN: 他干了一整周的活，拿到的报酬少得可怜。
senses.why: The word measures the distance between what a person needs and what is given; an amount that leaves the receiver wretched is called miserable by the same logic.
senses.whyCN: 这个词衡量的是人的需要与实际所得之间的距离；一笔让领取者陷入可怜处境的钱，按同样的逻辑就被叫作 miserable。

intro.en: Miserable comes from the Latin adjective miser, which named a person in wretched circumstances, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: miserable 来自拉丁语形容词 miser，本指身处悲惨境地的人，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Miser described someone wretched, pitiable or unfortunate, and it could also describe the circumstances that made a person so.
items.cn: miser 形容一个人悲惨、可怜、不幸，也能形容把人逼到这种境地的环境。

items.en: Miserabilis meant pitiable or causing pity, built from miser with the suffix -abilis, able to be.
items.cn: miserabilis 意为值得同情、令人怜悯的，由 miser 加表示「可被……的」后缀 -abilis 构成。

items.en: The verb miserari meant to pity or to bewail, and it kept the same root alive across the family.
items.cn: 动词 miserari 意为同情、哀叹，让同一个词根在整个词族中延续下来。

items.en: Old French took miserabilis as miserable, meaning wretched and deserving of pity, and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语把 miserabilis 写作 miserable，意为悲惨、值得同情，并把它传入英语。

items.en: Modern English widened the word from a pitiable person to bad weather, poor rooms and insultingly small sums of money.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词从「可怜的人」扩展到恶劣的天气、破旧的房间以及少得带侮辱意味的钱。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the family built on Latin miser plus one word that only shares its shape; the near-meaning group collects words for unhappiness and for bleak conditions.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在拉丁语 miser 上的词族，外加一个只在字形上相近的词；近义组收表示不快乐与荒凉处境的词。

entries.definition: In a wretched or unhappy way, from miserable plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以悲惨或不快的方式，由 miserable 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: A state of great unhappiness or suffering, built on the same Latin miser.
entries.definitionCN: 极度不快或受苦的状态，建立在同一个拉丁词 miser 上。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend money; it shares the Latin root miser but took the sense of a hoarder.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱的；与 miser 同根，但取了「囤积者」那一层意思。

entries.definition: To express sympathy for someone's misfortune, from Latin miser with com-.
entries.definitionCN: 对别人的不幸表示同情，由拉丁语 miser 加 com- 构成。

entries.definition: Very unhappy, or living in very bad conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 非常不快乐，或生活在极差的条件下。

entries.definition: Dark, sad and without hope.
Cold, empty and offering little comfort.
entries.definitionCN: 寒冷、空荡、几乎不给人安慰。

entries.definition: Depressing and showing no promise of improvement.
entries.definitionCN: 令人沮丧，看不到好转的希望。

normalIntro.en: The word rests on a Latin adjective for a wretched person; its family keeps returning to suffering, to the conditions that cause it, and to things that fall far short.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在一个形容可怜人的拉丁语形容词上，同族词反复回到痛苦、造成痛苦的环境，以及远远不够的东西。

normal.en: Miser in Latin named a wretched person, so miserable describes a person at the bottom of fortune before it describes weather.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 miser 指不幸的人，所以 miserable 先形容命运底部的人，之后才形容天气。

normal.en: The suffix -abilis in miserabilis marks what deserves pity, and French turned that adjective into the form English borrowed.
normal.cn: miserabilis 中的 -abilis 标记「值得同情」，法语把这个形容词变成英语借入的形式。

normal.en: Miserable keeps the same root as misery and miserly, though the three words went in different directions.
normal.cn: miserable 与 misery、miserly 同根，但这三个词各自走向了不同的意思。

normal.en: English says more miserable and most miserable rather than adding -er, because the adjective is too long for the short ending.
normal.cn: 英语说 more miserable 与 most miserable，而不加 -er，因为这个形容词太长，容不下短词尾。

normal.en: The word moves from a person to a room or a wage, so bad conditions and small amounts both inherit the same feeling.
normal.cn: 这个词从人移到房间或工资，于是恶劣的条件与微薄的数额都继承了同一种感受。

abstract.en: A wet coat under a leaking eave is the whole picture: misery felt on the skin before it is ever named.
abstract.cn: 漏屋檐下一件湿透的外套就是全部画面：苦难先是贴在皮肤上，然后才被叫出名字。

abstract.en: Miserable weather and a miserable wage feel alike because both leave a person with too little to live on.
abstract.cn: 恶劣的天气与少得可怜的工资感觉相似，因为两者都让人所获太少，难以度日。

abstract.en: The word turns a comparison into a feeling: whatever falls far below what a person needs is called miserable.
abstract.cn: 这个词把比较变成感受：凡是远低于一个人所需的东西，都被叫作 miserable。

examples.en: The refugees spent a miserable night in the leaking tent.
examples.cn: 难民们在一顶漏雨的帐篷里度过了一个悲惨的夜晚。

examples.en: The team played on through miserable weather.
examples.cn: 球队在恶劣的天气里继续比赛。

examples.en: He was paid a miserable sum for a whole week of work.
examples.cn: 他干了一整周的活，拿到的报酬少得可怜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「米则弱」——米少、人弱、心也苦；记住 miserable 是痛苦的、悲惨的。

root: 拉丁语 miser（可怜的、不幸的）派生 miserabilis（值得同情的），经古法语 miserable 进入英语；与 misery、miserly 同源，词根仍是「悲惨」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a person made wretched; the senses spread from that inner state to the conditions that cause it, to shabby places and things, and to amounts that fall far short.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个陷入悲惨处境的人；义项从这种内心状态扩到造成它的环境、破败的场所与物件，以及远远不够的数额。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure crouched under a leaking eave in the rain, clothes soaked through, shoulders shaking.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨里一个缩在破屋檐下的人，衣服湿透，肩膀一直发抖。

branches.en: a person shaking under a leaking eave
branches.cn: 在漏雨的屋檐下发抖的人

branches.en: a night spent in a flooded tent
branches.cn: 在进了水的帐篷里度过的一夜

branches.en: a room above a shop with one bare bulb
branches.cn: 商店楼上一间只有一只光灯泡的屋子

branches.en: a few coins counted twice at the end of a week
branches.cn: 周末把几枚硬币数了两遍

branches.en: a worker, a storm and a thin wage held in one frame
branches.cn: 工人、暴雨与薄薄一份工资收进同一幅画面

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin adjective for a wretched person, its suffix of pity, its verb, the French form and the English endings that build the adverb and the noun.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语中形容可怜人的形容词、表示怜悯的后缀与动词、法语形式，以及构成副词和名词的英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Miserable descends from one of the best recorded Latin families, the words built on miser, so the Latin side lists the adjective, its noun and its verb.
latinIntro.cn: miserable 来自记录最完整的拉丁词族之一，即由 miser 构成的那些词，因此拉丁同源部分列出形容词、名词与动词。

definition_zh: 效用；实用；公用事业；公共设施
definition_en: the quality of being useful, or a public service such as water, gas, or electricity
core_image: 墙上一排电表水表，各自记录着看不见的供给
scene: 老房子的墙角挂着一排水表电表，每月都有人来抄一次数字，账单随后寄到信箱。 Water is the most basic utility in any city.
sceneCN: 这里 utility 是「公用事业」（第 3 个义项：水、电、燃气这类公共服务）；句意为水是任何城市最基本的公用事业。墙角一排计量表的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「功利的；实用的」

senses.title: The quality of being useful
senses.definition: the quality of being useful or of practical value
senses.definitionCN: 有用或具有实际价值的性质
senses.example: The new tool's utility lies in its simple handle.
senses.exampleCN: 这件新工具的效用在于它那只简单的把手。
senses.why: The Latin noun joined utilis, useful, to the abstract ending -itas, so the word names usefulness as a measurable quality.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词由 utilis（有用的）加抽象词尾 -itas 构成，因此它把「有用」说成一种可以衡量的性质。

senses.title: The usefulness of something in a particular role
senses.definition: the particular purpose a thing can serve in practice
senses.definitionCN: 某物在实际情况中能充当的具体用途
senses.example: The old barn has lost its utility as a store.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧谷仓已经失去了储藏方面的功用。
senses.why: From usefulness in general the word narrows to the specific job a thing can still do.
senses.whyCN: 从一般的有用性出发，词义收窄到某物还能承担的那项具体职能。

senses.title: A public service such as water or power
senses.definition: an organisation or service supplying water, gas, electricity, or similar necessities
senses.definitionCN: 供应水、燃气、电力等必需品的机构或服务
senses.example: The city raised utility prices for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 市里提高了冬季的公用事业收费。
senses.why: Such services were seen as the most useful goods a town could own, so the abstract noun came to name the companies themselves.
senses.whyCN: 人们把这些服务看作城镇最该有的「有用之物」，于是这个抽象名词转而指供应它们的公司本身。

senses.title: A computer program for small tasks
senses.definition: a small program that performs a practical function in a computer system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机系统中完成某项实用功能的小程序
senses.example: The disk utility found the damaged file.
senses.exampleCN: 磁盘工具程序找到了那个损坏的文件。
senses.why: Software borrowed the word for programs whose whole worth is practical, echoing the oldest sense.
senses.whyCN: 软件领域借用了这个词，指那些价值完全在于实用的程序，恰好回应了最古老的那层意思。

senses.title: In economics, the satisfaction goods give
senses.definition: in economics, the satisfaction or benefit a person gets from a good
senses.definitionCN: 经济学中个人从商品中获得的满足或益处
senses.example: Economists measure utility rather than price.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家衡量的是效用，而不是价格。
senses.why: Economists made the abstract quality countable, turning usefulness into a quantity that choices can be weighed against.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家把这层抽象性质变得可以计量，让「有用」成为一种可供选择权衡的量。

intro.en: From Latin utilis, useful, through French; the abstract ending marks it as a noun of quality.
intro.cn: 来自拉丁语 utilis（有用的），经法语进入英语；抽象词尾表明它是一个表示性质的名词。

items.en: Utilis meant useful, from uti, to use, and utilitas named the quality just as bonitas named goodness.
items.cn: utilis 意为「有用的」，来自 uti（使用），utilitas 像 bonitas 表善那样表「有用」这种性质。

items.en: Utilité carried the abstract sense of usefulness into French legal and scholarly prose.
items.cn: utilité 把「有用性」这一抽象义带进法语的法律与学术文章。

items.en: Utility arrives in English in the fourteenth century, first meaning usefulness.
items.cn: utility 于十四世纪进入英语，最初只表示有用性。

items.en: From the nineteenth century, utility names the companies that supply water, gas, and power.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，utility 用来指供应水、燃气与电力的公司。

items.en: Economics and computing each take the word for a measured benefit and for a practical program.
items.cn: 经济学与计算机领域各自取用这个词，表可计量的效用与实用的程序。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the util- family, and the near-meaning group places usefulness beside value and service.
note.cn: 形近组收集 util- 词族，近义组把有用性与价值、服务放在一起。

entries.definition: to make practical use of
designed for use rather than beauty
plural, also the shares of such companies
entries.definitionCN: 公用事业；公用事业股票

entries.definition: to employ something
the quality of being helpful
a system supplying a public need
worth in use or exchange
something pleasant but not necessary

normalIntro.en: See util- as the useful stem and -ity as the abstract ending: usefulness turned into a noun.
normalIntro.cn: 把 util- 看成「有用」词干，把 -ity 看成抽象词尾：有用性做成了名词。

normal.en: Public utility names a company rather than a quality.
normal.cn: public utility 指的是公司，不是某种性质。

normal.en: Utility bill is the household phrase for water, gas, and power charges.
normal.cn: utility bill 是家里的水电煤气账单。

normal.en: Utilize and utility share one stem, one verb and one noun.
normal.cn: utilize 与 utility 同词干，一个是动词，一个是名词。

normal.en: A utility room is a plain working room, not a beautiful one.
normal.cn: utility room 是朴素的干活房，不是好看的房间。

normal.en: In economics the plural utilities is rarely used; the sense stays abstract.
normal.cn: 经济学里几乎不用复数，那一层意义始终是抽象的。

abstract.en: Picture a row of meters on a wall, quietly counting water and power.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上一排表，安静地数着水与电。

abstract.en: Open an envelope with a utility bill inside and see the winter figure.
abstract.cn: 拆开一个信封，看见里面冬季的水电单。

abstract.en: Watch a small disk program clean a cluttered drive.
abstract.cn: 看一个小小的磁盘程序清理杂乱的硬盘。

examples.en: The chief utility of the map is that it folds into a pocket.
examples.cn: 这张地图的主要实用之处是能折进口袋。

examples.en: The family cut its utility costs by half last winter.
examples.cn: 这家人在去年冬天把水电煤气费削减了一半。

examples.en: The building stands on land once owned by the local utility.
examples.cn: 这栋楼盖在曾属于当地公用事业公司的土地上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优体利体」——身体用起来又优又利，说的还是有用。

root: 拉丁语 uti（使用）→ utilis（有用的）→ utilitas（有用性），经古法语 utilité 进入英语

sensesIntro.en: The abstract quality of being useful narrows to a particular function, widens to public services, and is borrowed by computing and economics.
sensesIntro.cn: 「有用」这一抽象性质先收窄为具体功用，再扩大为公用事业，又被计算机与经济学术语借用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of meters counting invisible supply.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排计量表记录着看不见的供给。

branches.en: The quality branch: usefulness as a property of things.
branches.cn: 性质分支：作为事物属性的有用性。

branches.en: The function branch: the job a thing can still do.
branches.cn: 功用分支：某物还能担任的那项职能。

branches.en: The service branch: gas, water, and power as businesses.
branches.cn: 服务分支：作为企业的燃气、水与电力。

branches.en: The software branch: a program valued for its function.
branches.cn: 软件分支：以功能取胜的程序。

branches.en: The economic branch: usefulness made countable.
branches.cn: 经济分支：被变成可计量的用处。

intro.en: A Latin stem of use, a linking -il-, and the abstract ending -ity: usefulness as a noun.
intro.cn: 拉丁语「使用」词干，加连接成分 -il-，再加抽象词尾 -ity：把有用性做成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin uti, to use, gives utilis, useful, and utilitas, usefulness; the ending -itas becomes English -ity.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 uti（使用）给出 utilis（有用的）与 utilitas（有用性）；词尾 -itas 变成英语 -ity。

items.example: The verb uti is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 动词 uti 是整个词族的根。

items.example: The stem util- appears in utility and utilize.
items.exampleCN: 词干 util- 见于 utility 与 utilize。

items.example: Utilitarian adds a label for a way of thinking.
items.exampleCN: utilitarian 加上了思想取向的标签。

items.example: Utilization means the act of putting to use.
Use is the everyday cousin of uti.
items.exampleCN: use 是 uti 的日常对应词。

items.example: A public utility serves a whole town.
items.exampleCN: public utility 服务整个城镇。

definition_zh: 值得的；配得上的；可敬的；有价值的
definition_en: deserving something good, or having enough merit to be respected
core_image: 一件旧外套洗得发白、补过两次，但穿它的人站得很直
scene: 评选名单上，那个默默做了十年杂事的人排在最前面。 Her work with the children is worthy of more attention than it gets.
sceneCN: 这里 worthy 是「值得的、配得上的」（第 1 个义项：理应得到某种好的对待）；句意为她为孩子们所做的工作理应得到更多关注，而实际得到的太少。洗得发白却站得笔直的旧外套，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 要人；知名人士（多带调侃）

derivatives.zh: 由 worthy 加 -ness 构成，义为「值得；可贵之处」
由 worthy 加 -ly 构成，义为「值得地；相称地」
由 worthy 加前缀 un- 构成，义为「不值得的；不相称的」
由 praise 与 worthy 复合，义为「值得称赞的」

senses.title: Deserving of something
senses.definition: having enough value to deserve a particular good thing, as in worthy of praise
senses.definitionCN: 有价值到理应得到某种好的对待，如 worthy of praise
senses.example: Her work with the children is worthy of more attention than it gets.
senses.exampleCN: 她为孩子们所做的工作理应得到更多关注，而实际得到的太少。
senses.why: The root is worth, so the adjective says a person or thing has enough value to deserve its reward.
senses.whyCN: 词根是 worth，所以这个形容词表示某人某物有足够价值，理应得到那份回报。

senses.title: Respectable in itself
senses.definition: having the qualities that earned respect, often used of effort and character
senses.definitionCN: 具备赢来尊敬的那些品质，常用于努力与品性
senses.example: It is a worthy attempt even if it did not succeed.
senses.exampleCN: 即使没有成功，这也是一次可敬的尝试。
senses.why: The frame worthy of can drop its object, leaving the sense that the effort itself carries merit.
senses.whyCN: worthy of 的句式可以省去对象，留下「这份努力本身就有价值」的意思。

senses.title: The local notable
senses.definition: used as a noun, often with a touch of mockery, for a local person of standing
senses.definitionCN: 作名词用，常带一点调侃，指地方上有地位的人
senses.example: The town worthies gathered on the platform to give short speeches.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的头面人物都聚到台上做简短的讲话。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for people who are thought to embody worth, and the tone turns dry.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指被认为有分量的人，语气随之带上了干涩的调侃。

senses.title: Worth the trouble
senses.definition: used of a cause or a thing that justifies the effort put into it
senses.definitionCN: 用于值得为之付出的事业或事物
senses.example: The repair of the old bridge is a worthy cause for the whole village.
senses.exampleCN: 重修这座老桥是对整个村子都值得的一件事。
senses.why: Applied to a cause, the word answers the question whether the effort will be repaid.
senses.whyCN: 用到一件事上时，这个词回答的是「这份力气会不会有回报」。

intro.en: Worthy is Old English weorthig, worth plus the adjective ending -ig, then -y in modern spelling.
intro.cn: worthy 来自古英语 weorthig，即 worth 加形容词词尾 -ig，现代拼写变为 -y。

items.en: The adjective weorthig said that a thing had worth and so deserved regard.
items.cn: 形容词 weorthig 表示某物有价值，因而值得看重。

items.en: The ending weakened, giving worthy, and the noun use appeared.
items.cn: 词尾弱化，形成 worthy，名词用法也随之出现。

items.en: Worthy of became the standard frame for saying what is deserved.
items.cn: worthy of 成了表示「配得上」的标准句式。

items.en: In speech the adjective can sound a little stiff, which is why self-made uses poke fun.
items.cn: 口语中这个形容词略显板正，所以有些用法是拿来打趣的。

items.en: Unworthy and praiseworthy show how freely the word compounds.
items.cn: unworthy 与 praiseworthy 说明这个词复合得多么自由。

note.en: The first group holds the family around worth, the second holds adjectives of deserving and of respect.
note.cn: 第一组收 worth 周围的家族词，第二组收表示值得与可敬的形容词。

entries.definition: Value, or deserving of something.
The quality of deserving respect.
Not deserving, or not good enough.
Having earned good treatment.
Deserving respect and approval.
Of a good social standing, decent.

normalIntro.en: Worthy is worth plus y, with the comparison taking -ier and -iest.
normalIntro.cn: worthy 是 worth 加 -y，比较级和最高级分别用 -ier 与 -iest。

normal.en: The y turns to i in the comparison: worthier and worthiest.
normal.cn: 比较级里 y 变 i：worthier 与 worthiest。

normal.en: Worthy of is the frame: worthy of praise, worthy of note.
normal.cn: 常用框架是 worthy of：worthy of praise、worthy of note。

normal.en: Add un- for the opposite: unworthy of the honour.
normal.cn: 加 un- 得反义：unworthy of the honour。

normal.en: The ringing is voiced here, unlike the th in worth, because the ending is voiced too.
normal.cn: 这里的 th 发浊音，与 worth 的清音不同，因为词尾也是浊音。

normal.en: Praiseworthy and noteworthy are compounds, and both keep the y.
normal.cn: praiseworthy 与 noteworthy 都是复合词，都保留 y。

abstract.en: A coat washed pale and mended twice, worn by someone standing straight.
abstract.cn: 洗得发白、补过两次的外套，穿着它的人站得很直。

abstract.en: A name on a list placed above louder names.
abstract.cn: 名单上的一个名字排在更响的名字之上。

abstract.en: A hand held out to an opponent who fought well.
abstract.cn: 伸手递给一个打得好的对手。

examples.en: The plan is worthy of serious discussion.
examples.cn: 这个方案值得认真讨论。

examples.en: He is a worthy opponent and a fair player.
examples.cn: 他是个值得尊敬的对手，也打得公道。

examples.en: Teaching the children to read is a worthy cause.
examples.cn: 教孩子们读书是一件值得做的事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我值」——我「值」得这份尊敬，就是 worthy。

root: 古英语 weorthig = weorth（价值）+ -ig（形容词词尾，今作 -y）；比较级 worthier，反义 unworthy。

sensesIntro.en: Deserving a reward comes first, then being respectable in oneself, then the humorous use as a noun, and finally the cause worth doing for.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是理应得到回报，再是自身可敬，然后是带调侃的名词用法，最后是值得去做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mended coat worn by someone standing straight.
core.cn: 核心意象：补过的旧外套，穿着的人站得笔直。

branches.en: The deserving branch: work worthy of more attention.
branches.cn: 应得分支：理应得到更多关注的工作。

branches.en: The character branch: a worthy attempt that failed.
branches.cn: 品性分支：失败却可敬的尝试。

branches.en: The noun branch: town worthies giving speeches.
branches.cn: 名词分支：镇上头面人物讲话。

branches.en: The cause branch: repairing the old bridge.
branches.cn: 事业分支：重修老桥。

branches.en: The frame branch: worthy of plus a noun is the usual shape.
branches.cn: 句式分支：常用 worthy of 接名词。

intro.en: Worthy is a stem plus -y, and it still lives by the frame worthy of.
intro.cn: worthy 是词干加 -y，至今仍活在 worthy of 这个句式里。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic; the Latin words below express deserving with a different verb.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语；下面的拉丁词用另一个动词表达「值得」。
